For challenging physically tractable dimensions, it pairs each with specialized vision models that derive verifiable, physically grounded measurements, such as object-level 6D pose, metric scale, surface normals, kinematics, and numerical conservation-law residuals. It thus avoids relying solely on subjective scoring, while supporting both text-to-video and image-to-video generation. Finally, we validate the agreement between automatic metrics and human judgments through human evaluation. Meanwhile, we evaluate mainstream open-source and closed-source models and present several insights. By releasing the benchmark, prompts, and calibration protocol, we aim to foster physically grounded video generation.

items.title_en: Foundation Model Driven Optical Flow
items.abstract_en: We investigate how frozen pretrained visual and depth representations support dense optical flow when coupled with a supervised matching network. Building on TTSFlow, this paper studies Dense Prediction Transformer (DPT) feature decoding and one coarse-to-fine refinement stage. Our method fuses features from frozen DINOv2 and Depth Anything V2 models and estimates optical flow through a trainable transformer-based matching pipeline. After optical-flow training on FlyingChairs and FlyingThings3D, it achieves 2.37 endpoint error (EPE) on the Sintel training split, Final pass, compared with 2.52 for the FlowSeek (T) configuration reported here. Our RoCo-Spring 2026 entry, RoCo-29.VSAI, obtains a robustness-balanced score of 1.1038, Spring EPE of 1.411, and RobustSpring proxy EPE of 4.739, with a lower balanced score than seven of the twelve listed reference baselines. These results characterize the complete pipeline, which reuses frozen foundation backbones and performs one refinement stage. Code is available at: \url{https://github.com/Visual-and-Spatial-AI-Lab/FFlow}

items.title_en: BrushOff: Stroke-Based Re-rendering as a Watermark Removal Attack on Painting
items.abstract_en: Invisible watermarks are used to mark who owns a painting. We show that a simple attack removes the most robust one we test. The attack redraws the watermarked painting with brush strokes, using a pretrained stroke-based renderer. We call this attack BrushOff. It needs no training, no knowledge of the watermark, and no generative model. We test four watermarks on 500 paintings from five styles. VINE, a recent watermark built to survive image editing, survives all 14 conventional distortions we test, with at least 97.8% detection. Repainting lowers its detection to 1.8%, while the output keeps a no-reference quality score close to that of the clean paintings. Diffusion regeneration can also remove VINE, but at the same removal level it moves the image twice as far from the painting in DreamSim distance, and it changes what the painting shows. Because the renderer draws a countable number of strokes, we can control the attack strength step by step. Finally, we test what kind of signal survives. A simple probe that stores bits in the relative brightness of neighboring regions survives repainting, while a probe that uses absolute brightness does not. The same probe fails under diffusion regeneration, while VINE fails under repainting. Robustness to these two attacks is therefore a separate property, and benchmarks should test both.

items.title_en: From Short Clips to Real-Time Streams: Identity-Aware Supervision and Context-Efficient Generation for Video Face Swapping
items.abstract_en: Video face swapping transfers the reference identity to a target video while preserving its other attributes and motion. Despite recent progress in reference-guided flow-based methods, jointly achieving faithful identity transfer, high fidelity, and real-time generation over long video streams remains challenging. To address this challenge, we rethink the task-specific structure of reference-guided video face swapping. First, face swapping changes only identity while preserving most visual content, yet flow-matching supervision is weakly sensitive to these changes. We therefore develop Joint Rec-ID Loss, which balances explicit identity supervision and latent reconstruction according to the noise level. Second, the target video already provides non-edited attributes and temporal dynamics, enabling generation with fewer spatial tokens and shorter temporal contexts through Face-RoI Generation and Short-Context Rollout Training. By integrating these designs, we propose StreamingSwap, a reference-guided flow-matching framework for real-time streaming video face swapping. We also introduce HumanFaceVid, comprising 1,000 hours of cinematic training data and evaluation sets of 200 short and 200 long videos. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive identity transfer and visual quality at 20 FPS on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU, with stable generation over videos up to 10 minutes long. Project webpage: https://aim-uofa.github.io/StreamingSwap/

items.title_en: CaptionFuse: Training-Free Composed Product Retrieval Via VLM Intent Captioning and Weighted Embedding Fusion
items.abstract_en: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) retrieves products matching a reference image modified by natural language---a core capability for eCommerce search. Existing training-free methods fuse CLIP embeddings via arithmetic, but we identify a fundamental limitation: user text modifications are attribute-sparse---a user who types ``make it red with shorter sleeves'' specifies what to change but not what to keep (the floral pattern, the V-neck, the fit-and-flare silhouette). We introduce language-space fusion: a Vision-Language Model (VLM) jointly interprets the reference image and modification to generate a visually grounded product-title caption---e.g., ``Red floral fit-and-flare dress with short sleeves and V-neck''---that fills in the missing attributes from the image. Our method, CaptionFuse, requires no task-specific training and is model-agnostic. A controlled experiment confirms that attribute content--- not linguistic style---drives the gains: imperative and descriptive captions with identical attributes achieve equal R@10, while both outperform raw modifications by +6.5 points.

items.title_en: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
items.abstract_en: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active object-level 3D mapping. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection, cross-view association, geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets. Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions. Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9. These results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and constructing complete, precise metric maps. SpatialScout provides a quantitative testbed for developing agents that build reliable 3D spatial representations through active perception. Code is available at https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout.

items.title_en: Dual-Scale Condition-Shift Editing for Robust Real-World Image Demoiréing
items.abstract_en: Robust demoiréing of screen-recaptured images remains challenging: moiré varies in frequency, color, and spatial support across display-camera pairs and capture conditions. Dedicated restoration networks trained on finite paired data struggle with this diversity, especially when low-frequency color banding and high-frequency stripes co-occur. We present DemoiréEdit, a content-preserving editing framework that adapts the natural-image prior of a pretrained flow-matching editor to demoiréing. First, an endpoint-supervised training objective supplements velocity matching with pixel, perceptual, and frequency-domain restoration losses. Second, a dual-scale condition-shift strategy performs global correction at low resolution, then refines the image at full resolution by shifting the denoising condition from the first-stage output to the original input for detail recovery. We also introduce DailyMoiré130, a benchmark of challenging moiré in everyday screen photography, comprising 130 smartphone captures across diverse displays with low-frequency color banding, fine high-frequency stripes, and mixed-frequency interference. On the challenging DailyMoiré130 benchmark, our method achieves the lowest residual moiré area and receives 71.3% overall-quality preference in a blind Best-of-7 study with 31 participants. We also evaluate on paired FHDMi/UHDM, reducing residual moiré confidence by 47.1%/9.3% and increasing MUSIQ by 4.3%/2.0% over the best baseline for each metric.

items.title_en: Sensitivity and Identifiability of Tumor-Related Changes in Longitudinal Microwave Breast Imaging
items.abstract_en: Microwave imaging could monitor breast tumor response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, but between-visit changes in breast positioning and normal tissue may confound tumor-related changes. We use eight patient-specific dielectric models from longitudinal MRI of two patients at four time points. For each model, 24-port S-parameters were simulated from 1 to 3 GHz, and Jacobians computed for tumor permittivity and loss, fibroglandular tissue (FGT) permittivity, and breast rotation and translation. 1 mm positioning changes produced changes 20 to 50 times larger than a 10% tumor permittivity change above 2 GHz. Nevertheless, tumor sensitivity patterns were weakly aligned with positioning patterns, tumor-FGT similarity exceeded 0.8 at only some visits, and the Jacobians remained well conditioned. Tumor responses are thus small but separable; monitoring will require positioning correction, frequency selection, and noise-aware detectability analysis.

items.title_en: Scaling Vision Foundation Models for Toxicologic Pathology
items.title_zh: 扩展视觉基础模型用于毒理学病理学
items.abstract_en: Here, we present TOX-FM, a family of non-clinical PFMs trained on large-scale diverse histopathology datasets of over one million whole slide images consisting of over 60 organs across six animal species from over 14,000 toxicology studies across six decades. We introduce a comprehensive benchmark of 18 non-clinical downstream tasks, incorporate an established benchmark of 9 clinical downstream tasks, and evaluate TOX-FM against state-of-the-art clinical PFMs across both non-clinical and clinical domains. Notably, we explore open questions surrounding domain-specific training and cross-domain generalization, offering insights into the opportunities and challenges of applying PFMs in the non-clinical domain.

items.title_en: Drive2Gauss: FeedForward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction from Multimodal Generative Driving Videos
items.abstract_en: Generating reusable driving environments requires both controllable future observations and an explicit representation that supports rendering from different viewpoints, yet existing methods still recover explicit scenes from generated RGB videos through optimization for each sequence. To overcome these limitations, we present Drive2Gauss, a feedforward framework that converts jointly generated RGB, metric depth, and dynamic flow into dynamic 4D Gaussian scenes. A Multimodal Video Generator predicts the three modalities from reference multiview images and future control signals. Furthermore, we introduce a Gaussian Query Decoder that uses depth to initialize sparse 3D queries and flow to associate the queries across time, and integrates appearance information through spatiotemporal feature aggregation and iterative query refinement. The reconstruction stage operates in a single feedforward pass without optimization for each scene. Extensive results on nuScenes demonstrate that our approach attains an FID of 6.38 and an FVD of 12.43 for future RGB generation, a PSNR of 29.91 dB when reconstructing its generated observations, and supports both direct rendering under lateral camera shifts and downstream video fixing. Code and more visualizations are available at https://zttt04. github.io/Drive2Gauss_page/.

items.title_en: DenseHap: Dense Hand Haptic Estimation from Monocular Images
items.abstract_en: As dexterous robotic manipulation advances, scalable annotations of human hand-object interactions are becoming increasingly important. Furthermore, previous hand contact estimation methods suffered from issues such as dorsal-side misclassifications and insufficient precision, while lacking a unified framework for integrating multiple hand to environment interaction modalities, including distance fields, contact thresholds, and pressure. To address that, we present DenseHap, a unified end-to-end approach to estimate hand distance field recognition, comprehensive hand contact detection, hand pressure analysis, and hand reconstruction from a single monocular image. By incorporating three distinctly defined heads, along with a pretrained 3D reconstructed skeleton and an enhanced dataset, DenseHap outperforms previous state of the art models on four evaluation datasets, improving the F1 score by 8.5 percentage points (a 16% relative improvement) on untrained datasets and by 3 percentage points (5% relative improvement) on in-distribution datasets. Furthermore, DenseHap has effectively improved short-range hand estimate and pressure evaluation. Code and models will be publicly available upon the paper's acceptance.

items.title_en: PrismWAM: Decoupling State Representations in World Action Models
items.abstract_en: World Action Models (WAMs) typically represent the world through latent embeddings from pretrained video models, which entangle heterogeneous aspects of the world, from how it looks (e.g., texture and color) to how it is physically configured (e.g., occupancy and pose). This raises an underexplored question: $\textbf{what should constitute the state of a WAM?}$ We argue that the world state should separate how the world appears from how the world evolves under action: the former captures semantic context, while the latter is governed by physical state. To this end, we propose $\textbf{PrismWAM}$, which decouples physics from semantics while jointly modeling state and action. PrismWAM factorizes an embodied task into a $\mathrm{Semantic\ Planning}\rightarrow\mathrm{Physical\ Rollout}\rightarrow\mathrm{Executable\ Action}$ pipeline: given only the initial RGB observation, semantic planning learns to predict the final goal image, while physical rollout predicts the fine-grained evolution toward this goal in depth space; executable actions are then generated from the depth rollout. Without any embodied action pretraining or additional data augmentation, PrismWAM achieves strong manipulation performance in both simulation and the real world. Notably, PrismWAM even surpasses a broad range of models with large-scale embodied action pretraining (e.g., OpenWAM-$α$). More broadly, we reframe World Action Models from modeling how the world looks to how it responds to action, paving the way for action-centric world models grounded in occupancy, flow, tactile sensing, proprioception, and beyond.

items.title_en: MRI Reconstruction Risk Estimation from Inference Dynamics
items.abstract_en: Iterative MRI reconstructors produce intermediate estimates before returning a final image. We study these inference trajectories as a model-internal representation of realized reconstruction risk, measured by log-NMSE. Model-native states are projected to magnitude images, summarized by a fixed 16-dimensional descriptor, and mapped to risk using a source-trained ridge readout. Across three reconstruction backbones, trajectory features are strongly predictive of reconstruction risk on held-out source data. Under zero-shot target shift, their behavior is backbone-dependent, exhibiting both preserved positive association and readout reversal. Conditional analyses show that trajectory information can remain associated with error beyond an initialization-only predictor. A prefix analysis further shows that useful trajectory information can emerge before reconstruction completes. Repeated-mask and low-shot calibration studies indicate that trajectories primarily encode persistent case difficulty, while their orientation and calibration can change under domain shift.

items.title_en: Three-dimensional stochastic retinal models for synthetic eye-models
items.title_zh: 用于合成眼模型的三维随机视网膜模型
items.abstract_en: Purpose: Current eye models often assume a fixed spherical retinal curvature of 12 mm, which does not reflect the anatomical variability observed in vivo. This study proposes an extension incorporating the stochastic relationship between axial length and three-dimensional (3D) retinal curvature, enabling more realistic 3D eye models. Methods: Axial length and 3D retinal curvature data from 94 subjects, split into five subsets for cross-validation, were used to construct two probabilistic models: a Single Gaussian Model (SGM) and two-component Multi Gaussian Mixture Model (MGMM). Both were converted into conditional forms to estimate retinal curvature for a specific axial length, and evaluated against measured data distributions. Results: All models produced radii of curvature comparable to measured data (median difference 94% vs. >86%), but similar variance (worst f-test (p-value) 1.05 (0.71) vs. 1.05 (0.73)). Conditioned on axial length, both models performed similarly with overlap exceeding 93% and the worst f-test 1.02 (0.84). Given its simplicity and robustness, the conditional SGM was selected, achieving similar validation results: median difference ( 92%), and a non-significant worst f-test (1.02 (0.85)). Conclusions: The conditional SGM enables accurate generation of anatomically realistic 3D retinal curvatures based on axial length, supporting improved stochastic eye modeling for visual optics and population-based simulations of healthy eyes. Translational relevance: Replacing the fixed 12 mm retina assumption with a population-based stochastic model improves anatomical accuracy of eye models used in optical design and treatment planning.

items.title_en: Small Average Error, Wide Individual Error: General-Purpose LLMs Estimating Energy Intake from Meal Photos in a Feeding Trial
items.abstract_en: Photo-based estimation of food energy could ease dietary assessment, and general-purpose multimodal large language models (LLMs) make such estimates easy to obtain. Most evaluations use one photo taken before eating and compare with energy served, while dietary assessment needs energy eaten. We evaluated six models from two vendors (Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5; GPT-6 luna, 6.1 sol and 6 astra) on 802 meals from ACETADA, a controlled feeding trial with weighed intake, with the before photo only, before and after photos in separate calls (subtraction), or both photos in one request. Three results ran against intuition. Subtraction under-estimated intake for five of six models, because the models still report hundreds of kilocalories for a nearly empty tray. Scaling the before-only estimate by the average share eaten (0.87) matched much of the gain from the after photo; beyond that constant, the second photo lowered meal-level error by only 2.2 to 3.4 points, mainly in meals with food left. With one photo, two models had a near-zero intake bias only because they under-estimated the served energy and ignored uneaten food. In ablations, adding the after photo improved accuracy under both prompt formats for five models, while prompt effects varied across models. Over 148 feeding days, three models kept the 90% confidence interval of their mean error within a pre-set 10% margin, but no model reached the pre-set 30% limits of agreement. Protein was under-estimated by every model, most in protein-dense meals; repeated calls changed error by at most 1.4 points; a high reasoning effort helped only the smallest model (4.2 points) and changed the others by less than 1 point. A low average bias is not evidence of accurate individual intake estimation; such estimates should support, not replace, assessment by a dietitian.

items.title_en: Interpretable Face Contrast Modeling for Smartphone Portrait Rendering
items.abstract_en: The quality of smartphone portrait photography has become increasingly important to both manufacturers and users. Recent devices use complex computational pipelines to improve facial rendering under varied lighting. These pipelines vary widely across manufacturers, so the same portrait can look noticeably different across smartphones. These differences affect multiple aspects of facial appearance, making perceptual preference difficult to characterize with a single measure. To address this, we propose an interpretable framework that decomposes face contrast into three components: overall facial tonal separation, eye-region contrast, and micro-contrast of fine skin details. We formulate dedicated metrics for each component and validate them via pairwise human judgments, demonstrating that our approach correlates more closely with human contrast perception than traditional contrast measures. To support this analysis, we introduce a realistic mannequin-based dataset designed for systematic facial contrast evaluation, comprising 508 full-resolution captures from 29 smartphones under diverse lighting, with region-specific masks and extensive pairwise perceptual annotations. As a downstream analysis, we show that combining the three component-wise metrics provides a meaningful basis for modeling balanced facial contrast preference in a controlled setting, and we present a preliminary evaluation on a smaller real-portrait dataset indicating that insights derived from the mannequin study can extend to real images. Our work provides a controlled first step toward defining and evaluating face contrast in portrait imaging.

items.title_en: PDNet: Exploring Pruning and Distillation for Real-Time Worker Activity Recognition in Industrial Assembly
items.abstract_en: In this work, we address real-time fine-grained human activity recognition (HAR) in industrial assembly and introduce PDNet, a new framework that jointly exploits structured pruning and knowledge distillation for 3D convolutional networks. We start by training a 3D-CNN backbone in a supervised manner. Then, PDNet applies channel-wise structured pruning to obtain a more compact network. In the third step, our method is optimized using knowledge distillation from the large unpruned teacher to recover accuracy lost due to pruning. On the challenging MECCANO dataset with an X3D-M backbone, the pruned model without distillation reaches a Top-1 accuracy of 25.54 %, while PDNet raises this to 39.46 %, with only 6.90 MB model size and 3.78 GFLOPs. These results show that distillation within PDNet is highly effective in restoring pruned model performance and highlight its high potential for resource-constrained HAR in industrial assembly.

items.title_en: 3D Diffusion Models for Medical Imaging
items.title_zh: 面向医学影像的三维扩散模型
items.abstract_en: Generative deep learning methods such as Variational Autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks or Diffusion Models have achieved remarkable results in image synthesis. In particular, Diffusion Models have demonstrated superior image fidelity and sample diversity compared to other approaches on standard benchmarks, while also offering more flexible training dynamics as evidenced both in natural image domains and in medical applications. In medical imaging including Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging or Positron Emission Tomography, such models have various important use-cases including data augmentation, domain transfer, image reconstruction, inpainting, image augmentation and artifact correction. Further, generated images can be conditioned on patient characteristics, medical reports, segmentation masks or other images. Specific challenges arise due to the 3D volumetric nature of medical images, which translate to substantial demands in terms of memory, compute, and training data. This article provides a comparative overview of 3D Diffusion Models which have been developed for medical images, with a focus on current performance, limitations, and an outlook for future work.

items.title_en: YUTELA: A Scalable Edge Cloud AIoT System for Multi-Site Video Anomaly Detection with Scene Specific Adaptation
items.abstract_en: Building upon our previous Ancilia framework, this work presents \emph{YUTELA}, an edge--server--cloud AIoT system for long-term, multi-site video anomaly detection. YUTELA replaces workstation-based on-site processing with NVIDIA Jetson Thor edge devices and redesigns the multi-camera pipeline through camera batching and redistribution, shared memory, reduced inter-stage data transfer, task integration, and TensorRT-accelerated inference. It maintains a separate anomaly model per camera, retrained on a centralized GPU server once enough recent pseudo-normal data are collected, with updated weights returned to the edge. With eight cameras, TensorRT increases throughput from 14.17 to 29.94 FPS under normal density, and the optimized edge node exceeds the throughput of the workstation-based Ancilia system in seven of nine workload settings, reaching up to 2.03 times its throughput at extreme density. This gain comes at the cost of higher latency under lighter loads with four or eight streams. YUTELA was then operated continuously for 170 hours at four public sites using 31 existing CCTV cameras. The deployment shows that runtime load is driven by scene activity and input frame rate rather than by camera count, and that retraining frequency varies by about three times across sites. The 101 automatically triggered training events occupied only about 6.6\% of a single GPU, indicating that one global node can support adaptation for tens of sites. Mean end-to-end alert latency ranged from 6.8 to 15.4~s depending on site traffic and anomaly type. These results show that YUTELA enables practical multi-camera edge processing with low-cost, camera-specific adaptation across heterogeneous sites.

items.title_en: Progressive multi-scale tumor-state memory for incomplete multimodal brain tumor segmentation
items.abstract_en: Brain tumor segmentation uses complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences, but some sequences may be unavailable in practice. Their absence changes the information available for segmenting different tumor regions. Fusion methods can support different input subsets. However, fusion at several scales does not by itself specify how tumor evidence is retained and updated to guide fusion at later stages. We propose a progressive multi-scale tumor-state memory network (PMTM) for segmentation from any non-empty subset of T1ce, T1, FLAIR, and T2. PMTM maintains a compact state for the current subject across the encoder stages. At each stage, we use assignment maps to pool spatial features into ordered evidence vectors for each available modality. We average these vectors across the available modalities, and a learned gate combines this evidence with the previous state. The up- dated state guides residual fusion at that stage and is used in the state update at the next stage. A modality-token mixer also models interactions among the available modalities at each stage. We apply semantic supervision to the assignment maps at all four stages. We evaluate PMTM on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI across all 15 non-empty modality subsets. Averaged over the three tumor regions and the 15 subsets, PMTM achieves Dice scores of 75.31%, 77.54%, and 80.47% on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI, respectively. These scores are higher than those of RobustSeg, RFNet, and mmFormer in our experiments on each dataset. Component ablations and internal state analysis are performed on BraTS2020.

items.title_en: When Guidance Becomes a Guard: Early Interception of Unsafe Inputs in Text-to-Image Generation
items.abstract_en: Text-to-image diffusion models can produce unsafe content, while output filtering intervenes only after synthesis. We investigate whether native generation signals enable early detection of unsafe and adversarial inputs. We find that classifier-free guidance exposes strong safety signals in conditional responses, accessible through compact statistics and linear readouts. Based on this finding, we propose Conditional Semantic Trajectory Interception (CSTI), which aggregates activation contrasts between conditional and unconditional responses at early checkpoints for calibrated risk detection. CSTI fits concept-specific detectors using canonical concept and safe examples, without attack samples, intermediate image decoding, or generator modification. Across five generators, four adversarial attack collections, and two general NSFW datasets, CSTI achieves the strongest overall performance among six baselines at a matched 5% FPR. Early interception reduces generation latency by over 60% on intercepted paths. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of native conditional responses for early safety interception.

items.title_en: Long-form Video-to-Text Summarization using Recursive Language Models
items.abstract_en: While VideoLLMs have made significant progress in understanding short video benchmarks, they often struggle to summarize long-form ones. This is mainly due to performance degradation caused by long-context prompts, the inherent difficulty of preserving temporal continuity and a lack of semantically rich concepts in event descriptions. To tackle these issues, this paper introduces the first recursive Video Language Summarization Model (RVLSM) designed for video processing and tailored to long-form video-to-text summarization. RVLSM recursively decomposes videos into semantically coherent segments and delegates chunk-level reasoning to VideoLLM sub-models and external tools. It employs (1) Semantic Temporal Decomposition (STD), which preserves temporal coherence and continuity through a scene-aware chunking strategy that dynamically partitions videos according to semantic boundaries, and (2) Adaptive Multimodal Tool Calling (AMTC), which ensures semantic richness of the summary via a routing mechanism that selectively invokes auxiliary modules such as action recognition, optical character recognition, automatic speech recognition, and object detection. Experiments on the VideoXum and MixTyVSum benchmarks show that RVLSM consistently improves over zero-shot VideoLLM baselines across multiple model settings and performance metrics, and is competitive with a state-of-the-art fine-tuned model for video-to-text summarization. Importantly, the named entities in the RVLSM's summaries align more closely with those detected in the ground-truth summaries than those detected by baseline and state-of-the-art methods, confirming the saliency of the event descriptions it generates.

items.title_en: Policy-Adaptive Credit Assignment for Spatial Reasoning with Verifiable Rewards
items.abstract_en: Image-based spatial reasoning requires perception, decomposition, and inference, but the stage that limits accuracy can change during training. Answer-level rewards neither localize failures to individual stages nor provide discriminative group-relative feedback when all rollouts receive the same reward. Process supervision provides intermediate feedback, but fixed weights cannot adapt reward allocation to these changing bottlenecks. To address this gap, we propose CALIPER, an adaptive process-reward framework supported by SpatialTrace, a corpus of stage-decomposed spatial reasoning traces. CALIPER jointly estimates the associations between stage-wise reference coverage and answer correctness through within-group ridge regression, using these associations as utility proxies to gradually update reward weights. The resulting process reward supervises all rollout groups, including uniformly failing ones. Because utility estimates can become unreliable when answer-discriminative groups are scarce, a closed-loop harness monitors estimator reliability and validation performance to guide checkpoint rollback, rollout diversification, and early stopping. Extensive experiments across eight benchmarks and three backbones show that CALIPER achieves the highest mean under both one-shot and harness training, with consistent gains over fixed allocation across RL optimizers. Further analyses confirm the benefits of adaptive reward allocation and harness control, with favorable scaling in model/data size.

items.title_en: LaMER: Language-Conditioned Multi-Expert Routing for Weakly Supervised Referring Expression Comprehension
items.abstract_en: Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) localizes the image region described by a natural language expression, underpinning applications such as autonomous navigation, human-robot interaction, and medical image analysis. Under weak supervision, REC is challenged by the visual-linguistic semantic gap and the difficulty of inferring region-text correspondences from coarse image-level signals alone. Moreover, no single visual encoder captures all complementary properties---semantic alignment, fine-grained texture, and boundary awareness---while naively fusing multiple pretrained encoders yields heterogeneous, hard-to-reconcile representations. We propose LaMER, a weakly supervised REC framework that dynamically aggregates four frozen expert encoders through a language-conditioned Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module, adapting expert selection to each referring expression without instance-level bounding-box supervision. A Cell-Text Matching Head with Negative Anchor Augmentation, trained with a multi-objective loss combining contrastive, reconstruction, alignment, and load-balancing terms, further stabilizes optimization. LaMER achieves 77.67\%, 62.81\%, and 69.49\% Acc@IoU\(\geq 0.5\) on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg, surpassing DViN and WeakMCN by up to 16.49 and 14.49 points, with ablations validating each component.

items.title_en: One Fact, Many Places: Redundant Evidence in Long Visual Documents Breaks Single-Gold Evaluation of Retrieval, Citation and Attribution
items.abstract_en: Document understanding is increasingly judged on where an answer comes from, scored against annotated gold locations as if each fact lived in one place. In long visual documents, a fact often lives in several places: a chart value is restated in the text, a key figure reappears in the summary. We ask how often such copies occur in standard benchmarks and what they do to evaluation. We annotate 420 questions from MMLongBench-Doc and MMDocRAG with the locations that independently establish each required fact, checked by two independent reviewers. Copies are common and often cross-modal: 19.5% of MMLongBench-Doc test questions have a strict copy outside the gold, and in 28% of MMDocRAG questions a non-gold candidate alone supplies a required fact. Single-gold scoring then fails in three predictable ways. A retriever that finds a copy is scored as a miss: page recall@1 of text and visual retrievers is underestimated by 13-24 points on questions with a cross-page copy. A model that cites a copy is scored as citing wrongly: crediting equivalent evidence reverses 11% of pairwise orderings among 65 competitive MMDocRAG systems. Masking the gold region leaves the fact available elsewhere: with a copy in the input, 41-56% of correct answers across four models survive it yet fail once every annotated instance is masked. Set-level masking with automatically found copies closes 78% of the gap to masking every annotated instance at matched granularity (three models); an unverified key-string rule lowers survival at least as far but masks three times the area. We release the annotations and redundancy-aware metrics.

items.title_en: From Legacy to Contemporary: Scalable Color Modernization for Long Video
items.abstract_en: Bringing legacy video back to contemporary screens does not necessarily make it look contemporary. Earlier imaging pipelines often leave color casts, muted chroma, weak con- trast, and tonal imbalance, while correcting these character- istics still relies heavily on expert colorists and scales poorly to long, multi-shot videos. We formulate long video color modernization, a task that updates the chromatic and tonal appearance of legacy color footage while preserving scene content and coherence across frames and shots. We introduce a scalable, training-free framework that jointly modernizes grids of temporally adjacent keyframes using a pretrained text-guided image editing model, producing coherent con- temporary references without paired supervision. Compact shot-specific color transforms then propagate these adjust- ments throughout each shot, preserving spatial structure and temporal stability. We conduct a multidimensional evaluation on diverse legacy videos spanning five decades. We combine a human evaluation of perceived modernness with quantita- tive measures of content fidelity, temporal stability, percep- tual quality, and efficiency, and introduce Source-Weighted Inter-shot Grade Consistency (SW-IGC) to assess grade co- herence across shots. On our evaluation set, our frame- work achieves the highest perceived modernness while re- maining competitive across complementary measures, open- ing a path toward the systematic study of long video color modernization. Code is available at https://github.com/jiwoomood/ Video_Color_Modernization.git

items.title_en: HGASurv: Hierarchical Granularity-Aware Integration for Multimodal Survival Prediction
items.title_zh: HGASurv：面向多模态生存预测的层次化粒度感知集成
items.abstract_en: Objective: Multimodal survival prediction jointly analyzes histopathological whole-slide images (WSIs), genomic profiles, and clinical variables to stratify patients by risk. However, existing approaches often inadequately account for granularity differences across modalities, particularly in spatial organization and feature dimensionality. To address these challenges, we propose HGASurv, which introduces a hierarchical WSI encoding module and a clinical-guided graph propagation module for granularity-aware multimodal integration. Methods: The hierarchical WSI encoding module maps WSI patch features onto a spatial grid using their original coordinates and applies parallel convolutions to construct representations at patch, local-neighborhood, and regional scales. Genomic signature embeddings then query these scale-specific WSI representations through cross-modal co-attention, producing signature-conditioned morphological features. The clinical-guided graph propagation module uses clinical variables to define patient-similarity edges and propagates fused image-genomic node embeddings with graph attention, integrating clinical information through topology rather than feature concatenation. Results: Across three TCGA cohorts, HGASurv achieved the strongest overall C-index performance, with ablation studies supporting the complementary contributions of the hierarchical WSI encoding and clinical-guided graph propagation modules. Conclusion and Significance: By introducing hierarchical WSI encoding and clinical-guided graph propagation, HGASurv unifies multi-scale pathology representation with topology-based clinical integration in a hierarchical granularity-aware framework. This design shows that matching representation and integration mechanisms to modality-specific granularity improves multimodal survival prediction.

items.title_en: TriScore: Post-Hoc Out-of-Distribution Detection with Energy, Boundary Probes, and Transform Consistency
items.abstract_en: Post-hoc out-of-distribution detection usually relies on a single signal extracted from a frozen classifier, such as confidence, energy, features, or gradients. This dependence becomes fragile under classifier-level adversarial shift, where the shift can preserve the detector's chosen cue while changing the model's decision behavior. We investigate whether this failure mode can be mitigated by combining complementary detection criteria instead of selecting a single score. We introduce TriScore, a post-hoc OOD detector that combines three ID-calibrated signals from the same frozen backbone: an energy prior, a boundary-fragility score, and a transform-consistency score. These signals are standardized on ID validation data and fused by an input-dependent ID-residual gate, requiring no OOD labels, auxiliary model, training, or stored feature bank. Across four ImageNet-scale backbones, TriScore achieves the best mean AUROC among 15 post-hoc baselines under a non-adaptive adversarial-shift protocol, while remaining competitive on standard OOD benchmarks. Ablations show that the gains come from combining complementary cues rather than optimizing a single detector signal. These results support multi-criterion post-hoc detection as a practical route toward more robust OOD detection under classifier-level shift. The source code is publicly available at github.com/gursoyege/TriScore.

items.title_en: MCDA: Multi-View Graph Contrastive Learning with Dynamic Topology Augmentation for Functional MRI Analysis
items.abstract_en: Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) is a vital non-invasive tool for diagnosing brain disorders and uncovering pathological mechanisms. However, existing graph contrastive learning (GCL) methods often underexploit augmentation histories across training epochs and the relationships among different augmented views. In this paper, we introduce a topology-guided Multi-view graph Contrastive learning framework with Dynamic graph topology Augmentation (MCDA) for fMRI analysis. Unlike traditional GCL that uses fixed noise or edge-dropping, MCDA employs a Dynamic Augmentation Update (DAU) module that iteratively refines the augmented topology. Specifically, we incorporate self-aware and cross-sample augmentation strategies to simultaneously capture individual-specific functional signatures and inter-subject heterogeneity. We then design a topology-guided multi-view graph contrastive learning scheme that explores interrelationships not only between the original network and its augmented views, but also across different augmented views to maximize structural information preservation. We characterize the score-level optimization directions and establish a lower bound for the contrastive objective. The framework combines classification and contrastive losses for brain disorder diagnosis and examines discriminative functional connectivity patterns as potential biomarkers. Experiments on two public rs-fMRI datasets comprising 1,236 subjects demonstrate that MCDA outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. The code has been made publicly available at: \url{https://github.com/goodcodingagoodboy/MCDA}.

items.title_en: CARNet: End-to-End Coupled Association-Recognition Network for Fine-Grained Multi-Drone Collaborative Detection
items.abstract_en: Multi-drone collaborative detection aims to enhance target recognition by leveraging complementary observations from overlapping aerial viewpoints. Existing approaches typically follow a two-stage pipeline that first establishes cross-view correspondences and then performs fusion-based recognition. However, this decomposition suffers from inconsistent optimization objectives, redundant pairwise modeling, and irreversible error propagation, where incorrect associations inevitably undermine subsequent recognition performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose the Coupled Association-Recognition Network (CARNet), a unified framework that jointly optimizes cross-view target association and recognition fusion through a shared target-pair representation. To improve association reliability in densely populated scenes with visually similar targets, CARNet explicitly incorporates spatial cues into pairwise relation modeling. Moreover, we introduce two complementary causal-inspired intervention strategies: the first enhances cross-view association by emphasizing appearance-confusing pairs, while the second bolsters the robustness of fusion-based recognition by learning stable multi-view representations under incomplete visual evidence. In addition, we present MDMT-CD, a fine-grained extension of the MDMT dataset that enriches the original vehicle annotations with detailed category labels, providing the first benchmark specifically designed for multi-drone collaborative vehicle detection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CARNet consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. The MDMT-CD dataset and source code will be available at https://github.com/bigdreaming11/CARNet.

items.title_en: Localization Gains from Explanation Regularization Should Not Be Interpreted as Faithfulness Gains.
items.abstract_en: Training-time explanation regularization is often evaluated by whether saliency maps become more concentrated within annotated regions. We argue that this criterion alone is insufficient: transformation consistency, lesion localization, and faithfulness to the classifier are distinct properties and should be evaluated separately, particularly in medical imaging. We examine this distinction through a case study of Contrastive Grad-CAM Consistency (CGC) in three-class brain tumor MRI classification. Using a single-channel ResNet-50 with five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation, we compare a cross-entropy baseline with CGC. CGC changes overall Pointing Game (PG) from $27.24\%$ to $36.02\%$ and Relevance Mass Accuracy (RMA) from $11.17\%$ to $18.01\%$, while classification accuracy changes from $93.63\%$ to $94.87\%$. Perturbation-based faithfulness metrics show inconsistent changes: Insertion Area Under the Curve (IAUC) changes from $0.73$ to $0.78$, whereas Deletion Area Under the Curve (DAUC) favors the baseline ($0.36$ versus $0.41$; lower is better), and overall Iterative Removal Of Features (IROF) is $0.57$ for both models. These results support our position that improved spatial agreement with pathology should not be interpreted as a general improvement in explanation faithfulness. We therefore recommend property-specific evaluation in which the property targeted by the explanation objective, spatial agreement with reference regions, and model reliance are measured and reported separately.

items.title_en: From Cause to Effect: Generating Intermediate Event Chains in Videos
items.abstract_en: Video-Language Models (VLMs) excel at visual recognition but struggle with causal reasoning. Current evaluations are flawed: multiple-choice QA allows shortcuts, and open-ended QA lacks robust automatic evaluation. We introduce Causal Chain Generation (CCG), a novel task where models have to generate the sequence of intermediate events connecting a cause and an effect. This structured setup demands genuine reasoning and enables reliable automatic scoring. We accompany this task with two complementary metrics: SODA-Embedding, which measures the semantic matching of a generated chain against a reference, and Causal-QA, which probes the chain's causal coherence by asking whether it contains the specific causal facts needed to reconstruct the narrative. We provide two test sets: SF20K-CC, a manually annotated diagnostic on 20 short films, and CMD-CC, a movie clip benchmark derived from audio descriptions. Our analysis reveals that state-of-the-art VLMs struggle with narrative causality understanding, frequently hallucinating or omitting key events. To address this, we fine-tune VLMs with GRPO using a composite reward that combines a format reward, SODA-Embedding, and Causal-QA accuracy, demonstrating substantial improvements over strong baselines.

items.title_en: TIM: Temporal Decoupling with Iterative Mutual-Refinement Model for Longitudinal Radiology Report Generation
items.title_zh: TIM：面向纵向放射学报告生成的时间解耦与迭代互精炼模型
items.abstract_en: Automatic radiology report generation (RRG) aims to translate medical images into diagnostic text, reducing radiologists' workload and standardizing clinical documentation. Nonetheless, existing approaches mainly focus on single-timepoint analysis and fail to capture temporal disease evolution across longitudinal examinations. While recent longitudinal RRG (LRRG) approaches incorporate historical data, they often combine images from different time points within a single representation space, leading to blurred semantics and inconsistent temporal reasoning. In this work, we propose a Temporal Decoupling with Iterative Mutual-Refinement Model (TIM), a two-stage framework that explicitly decouples spatial pathology from temporal progression and iteratively refines reports through mutual feedback. Stage I performs temporal-decoupled representation learning, separating temporal evolution patterns from disease-specific features and generating radiology reports for both prior and current studies. Stage II introduces a mutual report refinement mechanism that identifies diagnostic inconsistencies within prior reports and iteratively rectifies both prior and current reports through error-sensitive feedback. Experiments on the Longitudinal-MIMIC dataset demonstrate that TIM surpasses existing single-image and longitudinal baselines, achieving new state-of-the-art performance across both language and clinical metrics. Code is available at https://github.com/yihengd/TIM.

items.title_en: Dynamics-Aware Sparse Attention for Efficient Autoregressive Video Diffusion
items.abstract_en: Autoregressive Diffusion Transformers have emerged as a powerful paradigm for long video generation. However, they are often constrained by prohibitive computational overhead and substantial memory footprints. This inefficiency arises from dense computation mechanisms that allocate uniform processing resources across all spatiotemporal regions, failing to leverage the inherent temporal redundancy of video where motion is typically confined to sparse areas. In this paper, we propose Dynamics-Aware Sparse Attention (DASA), a unified framework that shifts from dense computation to sparse, motion-driven generation to eliminate both storage and computational redundancies. Inspired by video codec principles, our approach explicitly decouples video content into dynamic and static regions. To mitigate memory bottlenecks, we selectively compress the historical KV cache by retaining only dynamic features within the generated chunk. Furthermore, to reduce computational overhead, we employ a region-level computation allocation strategy based on localized dynamics. Additionally, a dynamics-guided distillation method is introduced to enhance performance via a lightweight distillation training process. Experiments on VBench demonstrate that our approach accelerates autoregressive video generation by 2.16x, while preserving high visual fidelity.

items.title_en: XGLASS: X-Ray, Gaze and Language Assisted Slice Sequencing for CT Volumes
items.title_zh: XGLASS：用于CT体数据的X射线、视线与语言辅助切片排序
items.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve remarkable performance on 2D medical images, such as X-rays or pathology images, while 3D VLMs that directly process CT/MRI volumes lag behind due to limited 3D training data and the predominance of 2D foundation architectures. To leverage powerful 2D VLMs for analyzing medical volumes, which contain hundreds of slices, it is therefore necessary to focus only on those few slices, which are diagnostically relevant. To enable such a prioritization, we propose XGLASS, a method that transfers medical expertise from 2D X-rays to 3D CT for task-aware slice prioritization. XGLASS uses disease-conditioned importance maps derived from language-aligned radiologist gaze on X-rays and spatially aligns them with coronal CT projections, bringing gaze priors and CT content into a shared 2D representation. The fused gaze-prior/CT projection is then used to predict a disease-specific ordering of axial slices, prioritizing diagnostically relevant slices. XGLASS significantly improves budgeted retrieval over 2D and 3D-native baselines, achieving a top-10 hit rate up to 75.9% for the best-performing disease. In practice, this means that after inspecting only the top 10 slices (4.17% of a 240-slice scan), XGLASS identifies a diagnostically relevant slice in more than 75% of cases. For downstream slice-wise finding classification, an XGLASS-selected 30-slice candidate set reduces model calls by 87.5% while improving F1 by 11.3 percentage points over all-slice inference, 4.2 points over the strongest 2D selector, and remains competitive with 3D-native selectors while requiring up to 130.8 times less time and 10.9 times less GPU memory per finding, supporting its use as a lightweight preselector for volumetric CT analysis. The code and pretrained checkpoint are available on https://github.com/michaelgloeckler/XGLASS.

items.title_en: Spatially Informed and Direction Sensitive Representation Learning for Spatial Transcriptomics
items.title_zh: 面向空间转录组学的空间信息驱动与方向敏感的表示学习
items.abstract_en: Cellular states are shaped by both intrinsic gene expression programs and the spatial microenvironment in which cells reside. Spatial transcriptomics makes this context measurable, but effective representation learning requires capturing both spatially informative molecular signals and intercellular organization. Existing approaches address these challenges only partially: conventional gene selection can overlook spatially structured signals, while methods for encoding cell-cell relationships often either reduce a cell's microenvironment to proximity alone, discarding direction, or rely on absolute coordinates tied to an arbitrary tissue frame. Consequently, cells with similar neighbor distances but distinct spatial organization may receive overly similar representations, despite experiencing different biological contexts that shape their cellular states. We introduce Tessera, a spatial representation learning framework that addresses both molecular selection and cellular context. Tessera combines spatially informed gene selection with a geometric inductive bias that contextualizes each cell within its local tissue environment. By modeling relative cell-cell relationships, Tessera is translation-invariant while preserving direction, allowing neighboring cells to contribute differently according to their spatial context and cellular state. Across held-out tissues and technologies, Tessera outperforms existing spatial foundation models in representation quality and generalizes zero-shot to contexts up to $16\times$ larger than those seen during training.
items.abstract_zh: 细胞状态既由内在基因表达程序决定，也受其所处空间微环境影响。空间转录组学让这一背景可测，但有效的表示学习需同时捕捉具空间信息的分子信号与细胞间组织关系。现有方法只部分解决：传统基因选择可能忽略空间结构信号；编码细胞—细胞关系的方法或仅以邻近性代替微环境而丢弃方向，或依赖与任意组织坐标系绑定的绝对坐标。于是，邻居距离相似但空间组织不同的细胞，虽处不同生物学情境，仍可能得到过于相似的表示。作者提出 Tessera 框架，将空间信息驱动的基因选择与几何归纳偏置结合，把每个细胞置于局部组织环境中加以情境化。通过建模细胞间相对关系，Tessera 具平移不变性又保留方向，使邻居按各自空间情境与细胞状态产生不同贡献。在留出组织与技术平台上，其表示质量优于现有空间基础模型，并可零样本泛化到比训练时大 16 倍的情境。
items.highlight_zh: 保方向的相对几何建模微环境，零样本泛化至16倍大组织
items.digest_zh:
一、研究什么问题：空间转录组测序能同时给出每个细胞（或测序点）的基因表达和它在组织切片上的位置。要做下游分析（如聚类、识别细胞类型、发现空间结构），先得把每个细胞转成数值表示。难点有两处：一是选哪些基因——传统高变基因挑选常忽略「在空间上有结构」的信号；二是如何描述细胞的邻居环境——很多方法只看邻居多远，不看方向；或直接用绝对坐标，而组织切片怎么摆放是任意的，坐标系本身没有生物学含义。结果是：两个细胞邻居距离分布相同但空间排布不同，会被当成几乎一样，尽管它们所处的微环境其实不同。

二、用了什么方法：作者提出 Tessera。它有两块设计。第一块是「带空间信息的基因选择」，优先保留在空间上呈结构化模式的基因，而非只看表达方差。第二块是几何归纳偏置：不再用绝对坐标，而是建模细胞之间的相对关系，这样整体平移切片不改变结果（平移不变），同时保留方向信息，使位于不同方位、不同状态的邻居贡献不同的权重。

三、有什么结果：在未参与训练的组织样本和不同测序技术平台上，Tessera 的表征质量优于现有空间基础模型；更值得注意的是它能在完全没见过的、规模达训练时 16 倍大的组织情境下零样本工作。

四、为何重要：它把「选什么基因」和「如何刻画微环境」两件事统一起来，纠正了「只看到距离、看不到方位」的信息损失，为跨组织、跨平台的空间图谱分析提供了更可迁移的基础表示。

items.title_en: An Open Reliability Atlas of Sensitivity and Failure Modes in the Pulse Physiology Engine
items.title_zh: Pulse 生理引擎中敏感性与失效模式的开放可靠性图集
items.abstract_en: Pulse is an actively maintained open-source adult-physiology simulator, yet its maintainers report no formal sensitivity analysis of its operational inputs. We present the first open reliability atlas across its critical-care envelope: Morris elementary-effects sampling of seven inputs, four severity scenarios, male and female bodies (1,280 simulations). Sensitivity is skewed: three inputs carry a median 93% of each output's total. A four-flag classifier reveals failure modes: two operator-actionable, one sex-stratified. Tidal-volume oscillation (20.6% of runs) is consistent with patient-ventilator dyssynchrony; locking the VC-AC trigger to -2 cmH2O collapses that variability. At FiO2 = 1.0, transient hyperoxia makes 120-second runs underestimate plateau PaO2; 300-second healthy-lung reruns give a median 643 mmHg. Solver divergence was all-male in an input-extreme regime (20/1,280); reducing the male blood-volume baseline to the 4,082 mL floor eliminated it. Runs and flags are released openly, showing users which regions need checking before training on Pulse output.
items.abstract_zh: Pulse 是一个持续维护的开源成人生理模拟器，但其维护者称从未对其运行输入做过正式的敏感性分析。本文给出首个覆盖其危重症参数范围的开放可靠性图集：用 Morris 基本效应法抽样七个输入，覆盖四种严重程度场景与男女两种体型，共 1280 次仿真。敏感性高度偏斜：三个输入中位数承载了每个输出总敏感性的 93%。一个四标志分类器揭示了若干失效模式，其中两项可由操作者干预，一项与性别分层相关。潮气量振荡出现在 20.6% 的运行中，与患者—呼吸机不同步的表现一致；将 VC-AC 触发锁定在 −2 cmH2O 可消除该变异。在 FiO2 = 1.0 时，瞬时高氧使 120 秒运行低估平台期 PaO2；改为 300 秒的健康肺重跑后中位数为 643 mmHg。求解器发散全部发生在男性、且处于输入极值区间（20/1280）；将男性血容量基线降至 4082 mL 下限即可消除。运行记录与标志已公开，提示用户在用 Pulse 输出训练前应检查哪些区域。
items.highlight_zh: 首个开源生理模拟器敏感性图集，揭示可修复的失效模式
items.digest_zh:
一、研究什么问题：Pulse 是一个开源、仍在维护的成人生理仿真引擎，常被用来生成模拟生理数据（例如训练机器学习模型、测试临床决策算法）。但它的维护者承认，从未系统检验过「改哪个输入参数，会让输出变化多少」，也不知道在什么参数区间仿真会给出不可靠甚至崩溃的结果。没有这类可靠性地图，使用者可能把仿真伪影当作真实生理规律。

二、用了什么方法：作者在危重症参数范围内做全局敏感性分析。采用 Morris 基本效应抽样，考察七个输入参数，覆盖四种病情严重程度、男女两种身体模型，共 1280 次仿真。随后设计了一个四标志分类器，用来把异常运行归类为不同失效模式，并逐条追查成因与修正办法。

三、有什么结果：敏感性极度不均——仅三个输入就中位数贡献了各输出总敏感性的 93%，意味着多数参数其实不太重要，少数参数主导一切。失效模式方面：约 20.6% 的运行出现潮气量振荡，符合患者—呼吸机不同步的特征，把 VC-AC 触发值固定到 −2 cmH2O 后该变异消失；当 FiO2 = 1.0 时，短暂的过高氧分压会让 120 秒的短仿真低估平台期 PaO2，改为 300 秒重跑的健康肺病例中位数达 643 mmHg；求解器发散只出现在男性模型的输入极值区（20/1280），把男性血容量基线下调到 4082 mL 的下限即可消除。

四、为何重要：它把「这个仿真器哪里不能信」变成了公开、可复现的清单，并给出可操作的修复建议。对任何想用 Pulse 输出训练模型或做临床推断的人，这张图集相当于使用前的体检报告。

items.title_en: What I Disbelieve: Quantifying Belief With Negative Ranking Functions
items.title_zh: 我不信什么：用负排名函数量化信念
items.abstract_en: A challenge in exploring the psychology of human uncertainty is its measurement and quantification. Prior work has focused almost exclusively on probability, while the formal theories developed in philosophy are rarely tested. We tested Wolfgang Spohn's ranking theory, a normative account in which belief is graded by ordinal ranks of disbelief that combine by minimization rather than addition, as a descriptive model of human belief. Across six experiments, participants assigned ranks of disbelief to propositions involving personal experience, chance devices, sequential learning, and an Ellsberg urn. Ranks were reliable and, through the theory's two-sided rank function, distinguished belief, disbelief, and suspension of judgment. Participants respected the Law of Negation, never disbelieving both a proposition and its complement, in every task except a lottery. Disjunctions did not follow the theory's Law of Disjunction. Instead of taking the minimum rank of the disjuncts, participants averaged them. In a learning task, ranks aligned more closely than did subjective probabilities with objective probabilities. In an Ellsberg Urn scenario, the paradoxical behavior seen with betting was markedly reduced by ranks. We conclude that human belief has the bipolar, negation-respecting structure that ranking theory proposes, but combines disjuncts by averaging rather than by minimization. As a clear account of human belief dynamics with metrics that can be reliably measured, Ranking Theory provides a valuable framework for investigating and contrasting probabilistic and non-probabilistic accounts of human belief.
items.abstract_zh: 研究人类不确定性的心理学，难点在于测量与量化。以往工作几乎只关注概率，而哲学中发展的形式化理论很少被检验。本文检验 Wolfgang Spohn 的排名理论——一种以「不信」的序数等级来分级信念、并以取最小而非相加来组合的规范性理论——能否作为人类信念的描述性模型。六项实验中，被试对涉及亲身经历、随机装置、序列学习和 Ellsberg 罐的命题赋予不信等级。等级具有可靠性，并通过理论的双侧排名函数区分了相信、不信与悬置判断。除抽奖任务外，被试在所有任务中都遵守否定律，从不同时不信一个命题及其否定。析取项不遵循理论中的析取律：被试不是取析取项的最小等级，而是取平均。在学习任务中，排名比主观概率更贴近客观概率。在 Ellsberg 罐情境中，用等级时下注所见的悖论行为明显减少。结论是：人类信念具有排名理论所主张的双极、尊重否定的结构，但析取组合采用平均而非取最小。作为对人类信念动态的清晰刻画且指标可可靠测量，排名理论为研究并对比概率式与非概率式信念模型提供了有价值框架。
items.highlight_zh: 人类信念可用「不信等级」刻画，但析取取平均而非最小
items.digest_zh:
一、研究什么问题：人怎么表达「我有多相信某件事」？主流做法是让人报概率（如 70%）。但哲学里还有另一套形式理论——Spohn 的排名理论：信念不是用概率分级，而是用「不信的等级」编号，0 表示完全相信，数字越大表示越不信；它允许你既不相信也不不信（悬置判断），并用取最小值的规则来决定逻辑组合。这套理论此前几乎没有被拿来做心理学实验检验。

二、用了什么方法：六项实验，让被试给命题打「不信等级」。命题涵盖个人经历、随机装置（如掷骰子、抽奖）、序列学习（逐步获得证据后更新信念），以及经典的 Ellsberg 罐（涉及模糊性厌恶）。然后检查被试的等级是否满足理论规定的几条定律：否定律（不能同时不信一个命题和它的否定）、析取律（对「A 或 B」的信念等级应等于 A、B 中较小的那个），并与概率报告作对比。

三、有什么结果：等级测量本身很稳定。借助理论的双侧排名函数，可以清楚地区分相信、不信和悬置判断三种状态。被试在几乎所有任务中都遵守否定律——不会同时不信 A 和非 A（抽奖任务除外）。但析取律被违反了：面对「A 或 B」，被试不是取较小等级，而是把两个等级平均。在学习任务中，等级比主观概率更贴近客观概率；在 Ellsberg 罐中，改用等级作答后，原本用下注时才出现的悖论式行为大幅减少。

四、为何重要：它说明人类信念确实是「双极」的（有信与不信两个方向，且能悬置），这一点支持排名理论；同时也修正了理论：析取组合要用平均。更重要的是，它提供了一个不依赖概率、且测量可靠的替代框架，让研究者能更细致地比较「概率式」与「非概率式」两种人类信念模型。

items.title_en: Myo10-dependent leading-edge coordination maintains physical coherence of migrating dendritic cells
items.title_zh: Myo10 依赖的前沿协调维持迁移树突状细胞的物理连贯性
items.abstract_en: Dendritic cells (DCs) are the principal leukocytes responsible for priming T cells. DC migration though geometrically complex tissue environments is crucial for initiating robust and spatiotemporally coordinated activation of adaptive immune responses. However, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms that govern physical navigation of DCs remains incomplete. Here we identify the unconventional myosin Myo10 as a critical regulator of DC trafficking. We show that loss of Myo10 attenuates FITC-induced contact hypersensitivity and reduces the efficiency of in vivo DC migration and egress from dermal explants but notably has no effect on antigen uptake or in vitro T cell priming. We further find that the migration defects of Myo10-deficient cells are exacerbated by increasing geometrical complexity. Mechanistically, Myo10 promotes physical coherence and coordinated leading edge dynamics via its interaction with lamellipodin, which subsequently drives VASP-mediated actin polymerization. Together, our findings establish a vital Myo10-lamellipodin-VASP axis essential for spatiotemporal DC navigation through restrictive microenvironments, providing critical insights into the biophysical regulation of immune surveillance.
items.abstract_zh: 树突状细胞（DC）是负责启动 T 细胞应答的主要白细胞，其在几何复杂的组织环境中迁移，对启动稳健且时空协调的适应性免疫应答至关重要。然而，调控 DC 物理性导航的分子机制仍不清楚。本文鉴定非经典肌球蛋白 Myo10 是 DC 迁移的关键调控因子。Myo10 缺失会减弱 FITC 诱导的接触性超敏反应，降低体内 DC 迁移效率及从真皮外植体迁出的效率，但不影响抗原摄取或体外 T 细胞致敏。细胞迁移缺陷随几何复杂度增加而加剧。机制上，Myo10 通过与 lamellipodin 互作促进细胞物理连贯性与协调的前沿动态，进而驱动 VASP 介导的肌动蛋白聚合。研究确立了 Myo10–lamellipodin–VASP 轴对 DC 穿越受限微环境进行时空导航的必要性。
items.highlight_zh: 鉴定 Myo10–lamellipodin–VASP 轴驱动树突状细胞迁移
items.digest_zh: 研究问题：树突状细胞（DC）要穿过结构复杂的组织去启动 T 细胞，但细胞如何保持形体完整、让前端协同地向前爬行，机制一直不清楚。方法：作者用缺失 Myo10 的细胞与小鼠模型，结合接触性超敏反应、真皮外植体迁出、抗原摄取与体外 T 细胞致敏等实验，并在几何复杂度递增的环境中比较迁移能力。结果：缺失 Myo10 后，体内 DC 迁移与迁出效率下降、接触性超敏反应减弱，而抗原摄取与体外致敏能力不受影响；几何结构越复杂，迁移缺陷越明显。机制上，Myo10 与 lamellipodin 结合，进而驱动 VASP 介导的肌动蛋白聚合，使前端伪足动作协调、细胞保持物理连贯。意义：这说明免疫细胞的导航不只依赖化学信号，还依赖细胞骨架与力学层面的调控；该轴或可成为干预免疫细胞浸润的靶点。

items.title_en: Females do not avoid but prefer superparasitism in the parasitoid wasp Melittobia australica
items.title_zh: 雌性南方小蜂（Melittobia australica）并不回避、反而偏好过寄生
items.abstract_en: To reduce competition over limited resources, organisms often avoid resources already used by others. In parasitoid insects, females are generally expected to avoid parasitizing hosts already parasitized by other females, called superparasitism, and this prediction has been broadly supported across numerous species. However, in the parasitoid wasp Melittobia australica, multiple females were observed ovipositing on the same host despite the presence of nearby unparasitized hosts in the field. In this study, we first analysed field data using randomization tests, and found that females strongly aggregated on particular hosts rather than distributing randomly across hosts. We then conducted laboratory experiments to examine (1) whether this aggregation reflects an active preference for superparasitism and (2) whether such behaviour could improve parasitism efficiency. A choice experiment, in which females were provided with a parasitized and an unparasitized host, showed that females preferred superparasitism when hosts were non-diapausing. This result indicates that females of M. australica not only engage in superparasitism, but actively prefer parasitized hosts. Another experiment, in which varying numbers of females were allowed to oviposit on a host, found that offspring number per female decreased with increasing female number on diapausing hosts, whereas it remained constant irrespective of female number on non-diapausing hosts. This host-dependent result suggests that multiple females can more effectively paralyze vigorous non-diapausing hosts, thereby offsetting the negative effects of offspring competition. As Melittobia females are likely to attack non-diapausing hosts in most cases in the field, including those in the present study, this benefit of parasitism by multiple females may help explain their preference for superparasitism, in contrast to many other parasitoid species.
items.abstract_zh: 为减少对有限资源的竞争，生物通常会回避已被他人利用的资源。在寄生蜂中，雌性一般被认为会回避已被其他雌性寄生的寄主（即过寄生），这一预测在众多物种中得到广泛支持。然而在 Melittobia australica 中，野外观察到多只雌蜂在同一寄主上产卵，尽管附近存在未被寄生的寄主。本研究先用随机化检验分析野外数据，发现雌蜂强烈聚集于特定寄主，而非在各寄主间随机分布；随后通过室内实验检验：（1）这种聚集是否反映对过寄生的主动偏好；（2）该行为能否提高寄生效率。选择实验（同时提供已寄生与未寄生寄主）显示，当寄主为非滞育状态时雌蜂偏好过寄生，表明它们不仅会过寄生，还主动偏好已寄生寄主。另一实验改变雌蜂数量，发现滞育寄主上每雌后代数随雌蜂数增加而下降，而非滞育寄主上则保持恒定。
items.highlight_zh: 雌蜂主动偏好过寄生，可更有效麻痹非滞育寄主
items.digest_zh: 研究问题：寄生蜂雌性通常被认为会回避已被别的雌蜂寄生的寄主（过寄生），以免后代争夺有限资源。但野外观察发现，Melittobia australica 的多只雌蜂会在同一寄主上产卵，附近明明还有未被寄生的寄主。方法：作者先用随机化检验分析野外数据，判断雌蜂是随机分布还是聚集；再用室内选择实验（同时提供已寄生与未寄生寄主）检验是否存在主动偏好；最后让不同数量的雌蜂在同一寄主上产卵，统计每雌后代数。结果：野外雌蜂明显聚集于特定寄主；选择实验中，当寄主处于非滞育状态时雌蜂偏好已寄生寄主；后代数方面，滞育寄主上每雌后代随雌蜂数增加而减少，非滞育寄主上则基本不变。解释与意义：非滞育寄主更强壮，多只雌蜂协作能更有效地将其麻痹，从而抵消后代竞争带来的损失。这挑战了过寄生总应被回避的经典预期，说明寄主状态会改变合作与竞争之间的平衡。

items.title_en: Integrating Multisource Target Evidence with Machine-Learning Potency Prediction for Alzheimer's Disease Drug Discovery
items.title_zh: 整合多源靶点证据与机器学习活性预测用于阿尔茨海默病药物发现
items.abstract_en: Alzheimer's disease (AD) target evidence is distributed across biological, chemical, structural, regulatory, and trial-registry sources, complicating reproducible target evaluation and modeling. We developed a traceable data-to-model platform that integrates AGORA-centered evidence through Target Explorer, Drug-Target Lookup, and Model Portfolio workspaces. The resource contains 967 targets, 452,249 compounds, and 1,430,260 measurements. On a curated PIK3CA dataset, target-specific fine-tuning of the Boltz-2 affinity head increased Pearson r from 0.248 to 0.560 and reduced mean absolute error from 0.900 to 0.706 on 469 held-out compounds. Separately, we screened 42 regression models over 50 random splits for ten moderate-sized target datasets; a random forest model for XDH achieved the highest mean R^2 (0.815). The platform connects curated evidence, model-ready datasets, reproducible evaluation, and public results while clearly separating contextual evidence from therapeutic claims and random-split performance from generalization to unseen chemical scaffolds.
items.abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（AD）的靶点证据分散于生物学、化学、结构、调控与临床试验注册等多类来源，使可重复的靶点评估与建模变得困难。我们开发了可追溯的“数据到模型”平台，通过 Target Explorer、Drug-Target Lookup 与 Model Portfolio 工作区整合以 AGORA 为中心的证据，涵盖 967 个靶点、452,249 个化合物与 1,430,260 条测量数据。在精选的 PIK3CA 数据集上，对 Boltz-2 亲和力预测头进行靶点特异微调，使 469 个留出化合物上的 Pearson r 由 0.248 提升至 0.560，平均绝对误差由 0.900 降至 0.706。此外，我们针对十个中等规模靶点数据集，在 50 次随机划分上筛选 42 个回归模型，XDH 的随机森林模型取得最高平均 R²（0.815）。该平台将整理后的证据、可用于建模的数据集、可重复评估与公开结果连接起来，同时明确区分背景证据与治疗主张，并区分随机划分表现与对未见化学骨架的泛化能力。
items.highlight_zh: 可追溯平台整合 AD 靶点证据并提升活性预测精度
items.digest_zh: 研究问题：阿尔茨海默病药物研发需要评估靶点，但证据散落在生物学、化学、结构、通路调控和临床试验登记等来源，难以可复现地比较与建模。方法：作者搭建可追溯的“数据到模型”平台，以 AGORA 为核心，通过 Target Explorer、Drug-Target Lookup 和 Model Portfolio 三个工作区，把靶点证据、化合物与活性测量整合起来。结果：平台收录 967 个靶点、约 45 万个化合物、143 万条测量。在精选的 PIK3CA 数据上，对 Boltz-2 的亲和力预测头做靶点特异微调后，469 个留出化合物的 Pearson 相关系数从 0.248 升到 0.560，平均绝对误差从 0.900 降到 0.706。另在十个中等规模靶点数据集上比较 42 种回归模型、各做 50 次随机划分，XDH 的随机森林平均 R² 最高，为 0.815。意义：平台把零散证据变成可复现的建模流程，并明确区分背景证据与治疗结论、随机划分表现与对新化学骨架的泛化，有助于减少靶点研究中的乐观偏差。

items.title_en: Glucose restriction reduces systemic, but not cardiac, inflammation during neonatal sepsis in preterm pigs
items.title_zh: 葡萄糖限制减轻早产猪新生儿脓毒症期间的全身炎症，但不减轻心脏炎症
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Preterm infants are highly susceptible to sepsis and hyperglycemia may exacerbate inflammation and worsen outcomes. We examined how glucose provision influences systemic and cardiac responses during neonatal sepsis in preterm pigs. Methods: Preterm piglets (90 % gestation) were infused with Staphylococcus epidermidis to induce sepsis. In Experiment 1, three ventilated and anesthetized piglets were continuously monitored for mean arterial pressure (MAP) and blood gases to characterize acute cardiovascular and metabolic deterioration. In Experiment 2, thirty-three piglets were randomized to standard (14 g/kg/day) or reduced (3.5 g/kg/day) glucose provision, with or without infection, and followed for 20h. Results: Infection in Experiment 1 caused progressive hypotension, acidosis, and hypoxia, mirroring clinical neonatal sepsis. In Experiment 2, reduced glucose provision improved survival (77 % vs 46 %, p = 0.06) and attenuated systemic inflammation, with lower IL-6 and higher IL-10 concentrations. Infection induced mild cardiac neutrophil infiltration, without affecting plasma troponin T but clearly reduced cardiomyocyte mitotic density and triggered upregulation of inflammatory transcriptional pathways (NF-{kappa}B, JAK-STAT) and suppression of oxidative phosphorylation. In infected animals. glucose restriction preserved cardiomyocyte mitotic density but did not alter cardiac structure, injury markers or gene expression. Conclusion: Neonatal infection induced circulatory failure, suppression of cardiomyocyte proliferation and upregulation of inflammatory genes in cardiac tissue, while reduced glucose provision mitigated systemic immune responses and preserved cardiomyocyte proliferation.

items.title_en: Resistance Training Frequency and Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Volume-Equated Trials
items.title_zh: 抗阻训练频率与肌肉肥大：等容量试验的系统综述与荟萃分析
items.abstract_en: Weekly training volume is the primary driver of resistance-training hypertrophy, but the independent role of frequency can be isolated only when weekly volume is equated. We quantified the effect of training frequency on hypertrophy across one to three volume-equated sessions per muscle per week. Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched to October 2026 for trials of at least six weeks that equated weekly volume between per-muscle frequencies and measured muscle size. One change-score standardized mean difference per trial (Hedges g; negative favoring higher frequency) was pooled with a random-effects model, and certainty was rated with GRADE. Sixteen trials (380 participants) were pooled. The frequency effect was trivial and non-significant (g = -0.02; 95% CI -0.21 to 0.16; I{superscript 2} = 0%; prediction interval -0.23 to 0.18); the interval admits at most a small effect favoring the higher frequency. Contrast-specific estimates were similarly trivial, and no moderator was significant, although the moderator analyses could detect only large effects. Certainty was low to very low. Within this range, the data give no basis for preferring one, two or three sessions at a fixed weekly volume. Most trials measured muscle thickness, which does not track whole-muscle growth reliably.

items.title_en: Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model Deployment for Oncology Registry Abstraction: Structure-Aware Evaluation in a Real-World Clinical Setting
items.title_zh: 面向肿瘤登记数据抽象的隐私保护大语言模型部署：真实世界临床环境中的结构感知评估
items.abstract_en: Objectives Structuring oncology clinical notes into registry-grade variables is essential for research and care but remains labour-intensive and error-prone. This study developed and evaluated a privacy-preserving large language model pipeline for oncology registry abstraction in a real-world clinical setting. Methods An open-source Meta Llama 3.3 70B-based pipeline, prompted without task-specific fine-tuning, was deployed to extract over 50 variables from 6,700 oncology notes at a cancer centre in Singapore. Data were de-identified locally using a Hide-In-Plain-Sight approach, ensuring no identifiable data left hospital infrastructure. Performance was assessed on 200 randomly sampled notes with adjudicated ground truth, using a structure-aware framework that classified outputs as correct, missing, spurious, or incorrect. Results F1 scores were high across variables, including diagnosis (97.2%), histology (95.8%), stage (92.6%), biomarkers (91.4%), and treatments (88.1%). Preliminary transferability testing on 50 external notes showed strong performance for core diagnostic variables, with reduced performance for list-valued variables. Discussion The structure-aware evaluation approach separated omissions from fabrications, providing more clinically actionable insight than aggregate metrics alone. Conclusion Privacy-preserving large language models achieved high extraction accuracy under a clinician-verified reference standard, supporting their feasibility for oncology registry abstraction in real-world clinical settings. Keywords: Large language models; Oncology registry abstraction; Natural language processing; Privacy-preserving AI; Clinical data extraction What is already known on this topic Structuring oncology clinical notes into registry-grade variables is essential for cancer research and care but remains labour-intensive, costly, and inconsistent from one reviewer to the next when performed manually. Large language models offer potential to automate this task, but their use in real-world registries has been limited by concerns over patient data privacy, reliance on task-specific fine-tuning, and evaluation methods that obscure the difference between missing and fabricated information. What this study adds This study shows that an open-source, privacy-preserving large language model pipeline, deployed entirely within hospital infrastructure without task-specific fine-tuning, can extract over 50 registry variables from oncology notes with high accuracy (F1 scores 88-97% across key variables), validated against ground truth checked by two clinicians. Using a structure-aware evaluation framework, we demonstrate that errors can be meaningfully separated into missing, spurious, and incorrect categories, offering clearer insight into model behaviour than aggregate accuracy metrics alone, and show preliminary evidence of transferability to notes from an external setting. How this study might affect research, practice or policy These findings support the feasibility of deploying privacy-preserving, locally hosted large language models for oncology registry abstraction without requiring identifiable data to leave hospital systems or extensive model customisation. The structure-aware evaluation framework is also shared as a reusable template, enabling other institutions to validate similar AI extraction tools in a consistent, clinically meaningful way before wider implementation.

items.title_en: Sustained Viral Suppression and its association with Psychiatric Morbidity and Sleep Quality among Older Adults with Human Immunodeficiency Virus: Evidence from a Retrospective Cohort in Ibadan, Nigeria.
items.title_zh: 持续病毒抑制及其与人类免疫缺陷病毒老年感染者精神疾病患病率和睡眠质量的关联：来自尼日利亚伊巴丹回顾性队列的证据
items.abstract_en: PurposeOlder adults with HIV are at risk of psychiatric disorders and poor sleep quality, but evidence from sub-Saharan Africa is limited, particularly regarding sustained viral suppression. This study examined the prevalence of psychiatric disorders and poor sleep quality symptoms and their association with sustained viral suppression among older adults with HIV in Nigeria. MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted among older adults receiving care at a tertiary HIV clinic in Ibadan, Nigeria. Viral load data from 2019-2023 were abstracted from medical records to determine sustained viral load suppression, while psychiatric morbidity and sleep quality were assessed cross-sectionally in 2023. Psychiatric assessments included major depressive disorder, anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder and mania. Mixed-effects logistic regression assessed changes in viral suppression over time and associations with psychiatric morbidity and sleep quality. ResultsAmong 400 participants, 63.5% were female and mean age was 58.2 years ({+/-} 6.5). A total of 25.8% had major depressive disorder, 17.5% had anxiety disorder, 29.3% had poor sleep quality, 3.3%, bipolar disorder, and 1.0% mania. Viral suppression improved significantly over the retrospective period. Sustained viral suppression was significantly associated with higher odds of good sleep quality (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.07-2.66, p = 0.025), but not psychiatric morbidity. ConclusionPsychiatric disorders and poor sleep quality are common among older adults with HIV in Nigeria. Sustained viral suppression was associated with better sleep quality but not psychiatric morbidity highlighting the importance of integrating mental health and sleep assessment into comprehensive HIV care for older adults.

items.title_en: Convergent and Divergent Neural Signatures of Cue-Induced Response in Substance and Behavioral Addictions: A Coordinate-Based Neuroimaging Meta-Analysis
items.title_zh: 物质成瘾与行为成瘾中线索诱发反应的趋同与趋异神经特征：基于坐标的神经影像荟萃分析
items.abstract_en: Addiction-related cues trigger craving and precipitate relapse, yet whether substance use disorders (SUDs) and behavioral addictions (BAs) share a universal neurobiological cue-reactivity core remains unresolved. We conducted a coordinate-based meta-analysis using Seed-based d Mapping with Permutation of Subject Images (SDM-PSI) to synthesize whole-brain fMRI studies comparing visually evoked cue-reactivity in strictly diagnosed SUDs and BAs versus healthy controls. An updated systematic search through September 12, 2026, yielded 50 eligible articles comprising 53 independent contrasts and 2,578 participants. Pooled analyses across all addictions revealed convergent cue-elicited activations in the mid-cingulate cortex, precentral gyrus, and a midline midbrain region. However, a formal SUD {cap} BA conjunction analysis yielded no family-wise error (FWE)-corrected shared clusters. Direct comparisons demonstrated greater activation in the left hippocampus, pregenual anterior cingulate cortex, and precuneus for SUDs relative to BAs. Importantly, the left hippocampal and precuneus differences survived age adjustment; furthermore, the hippocampal finding remained robust when restricting analyses to highly controlled cue-versus-neutral paradigms, while the precuneus finding was retained within picture-cue modalities.
