items.title_en: The Four-Qubit Hyperbolic Quadric Has Contextuality Degree 315
items.abstract_en: The contextuality degree of a set of Pauli contexts is the least number of contexts that every noncontextual $\pm1$ assignment violates. For the four-qubit hyperbolic quadric $\mathcal{Q}^{+}(7,2)$, with $135$ points and $1575$ lines as contexts, Muller et al. conjectured from heuristic searches that the degree is $315$ and that the violated contexts of every optimal assignment form a dual polar space $DW(5,2)$. We prove both conjectures. The lower bound has a short proof by hand: every doily ($GQ(2,2)$) of the quadric contains ten Peres-Mermin grids covering each of its lines four times, so every assignment violates at least three of its fifteen lines, and averaging over the doilies gives $1575/5=315$. The equality case is local: an assignment is optimal exactly when it violates one ruling of one grid in every doily. Using this as a SAT encoding, we show that there are exactly $240$ optimal violated sets, one orbit of $\mathrm{O}^+(8,2)$, each isomorphic to $DW(5,2)$. The same argument gives the first lower bounds $\lceil L/5\rceil$ for all quadrics with $L$ lines in $N\ge4$ qubits. The degree theorem is kernel-checked in Lean 4, and the completeness of the enumeration is certified by a DRAT proof checked by the verified checker cake_lpr.

items.title_en: Giant Rydberg Excitons Delineated as Relativistic Bound States
items.abstract_en: We examined the energy-momentum relationship of the valence band of Cu$_2$O, which has gained interest as an emerging solid host for giant Rydberg states. Our findings reveal a nonparabolic dispersion, described using the rest mass (0.570 times the free electron mass) and rescaled light speed ($1.6\times 10^5$ m/s), which draws parallels with relativistic theory for high-energy particles. We propose a straightforward expression for the bound-state energies of Rydberg excitons with finite quantum defects, whose energy scheme deviates from the hydrogenic series. This formulation identifies relativistic kinematics as the physical origin of quantum defects, offering a streamlined basis for future studies on complex many-body correlations.

items.title_en: Parameter-efficient neural computing with programmable photonic meshes
items.title_zh: 基于可编程光子网格的参数高效神经计算
items.abstract_en: Memory capacity and bandwidth are becoming major constraints in neural-network computing, motivating parameter-efficient representations that reduce model storage and data movement. Tensor-network methods already enable substantial compression of neural networks, but their structured operations are often poorly matched to conventional processors optimized for dense linear algebra. Such representations can be implemented in photonic hardware, although this typically requires optical architectures tailored to a particular factorization. Here we propose a different approach based on programmable photonic meshes. Compact electronic parameters determine the interferometer phases, while optical interference produces a dense, generally high-rank transformation. Since the parameterization remains electronic, its dimensionality and structure can be changed without modifying the optical circuit. Numerical experiments in end-to-end training demonstrate that the proposed photonic layers match or outperform strongly compressed tensor-train and brickwork layers, often with fewer trainable parameters. Experiments in parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a language model also show advantages over established digital adapters. The reduced trainable state lowers persistent memory requirements and offers the potential to reduce data movement and bandwidth demands.

items.title_en: Two-qubit cryo-CMOS control of a spin register in diamond
items.abstract_en: Utility-scale quantum technologies will not only require a well-performing quantum platform, but also classical control hardware that is scalable, efficient, and meets the design requirements set by the quantum system of interest. One approach is the application of silicon CMOS technology, a highly scalable and mature technology, to design application-specific integrated circuits (ASIC) that are optimized for the quantum system. In this work, we present two-qubit control of electron and nuclear spins in NV centres in diamond, using a cryogenic CMOS qubit controller integrated with a diamond quantum device in a cryostat. Using Gate Set Tomography (GST) we characterize the performance of the single-qubit gates on both electron- and carbon nuclear spins, and analyze the limiting noise processes. We use dynamical decoupling to engineer a two-qubit gate, and estimate $F_\text{2q,avg} = 95(2)\%$ for the electron-nuclear two-qubit gate fidelity. Our demonstration of cryo-CMOS-driven two-qubit gates is a key step towards highly-integrated quantum devices based on colour centres.

items.title_en: Higher-order Parity Constraints for Quantum Approximate Optimization
items.abstract_en: The Parity Architecture was originally introduced in the context of quantum optimization algorithms to overcome hardware connectivity constraints. Here, we show that its benefits extend beyond this role by identifying specific parity transformations that enhance the success probability of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for optimization problems defined on hardware-native and sparse graphs. Numerical simulations suggest that this enhancement originates from the higher-order operators introduced by the Parity representation, which accelerate the propagation of correlations across the physical device. We investigate this mechanism for the Signed Max-Cut problem on 3-regular graph instances and demonstrate its practical relevance on IBM Heron quantum processors. QAOA parameters are first classically optimized on small training instances containing up to 14 vertices and subsequently transferred to larger instances executed on quantum hardware. We consider Signed Max-Cut instances of up to 40 vertices and find that, together with an error mitigation technique, the parity-based QAOA identifies the optimal solutions for all the considered 40-vertex instances, whereas the conventional QAOA fails under the same conditions.

items.title_en: Self-Oscillating Photonic Frequency Comb for Sub-THz Local Oscillator Generation in Earth Observation Systems
items.abstract_en: Earth observation missions rely on microwave and sub-terahertz radiometry for retrieving atmospheric parameters such as temperature, humidity, and cloud properties, with the 183- and 229-GHz spectral regions being particularly relevant. Local-oscillator (LO) generation at these frequencies requires low phase noise and high frequency stability while meeting stringent size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints. Conventional architectures employ dielectric resonator oscillators followed by cascaded frequency-multiplication stages, requiring dedicated generation chains for different frequency bands and increasing hardware complexity. Furthermore, frequency multiplication degrades the phase noise of the generated signal. This work proposes and numerically investigates a reconfigurable self-oscillating microwave photonic architecture for LO generation in Earth observation receivers. Cascaded Mach-Zehnder and phase modulation within an optoelectronic feedback loop generate an optical frequency comb with enhanced higher-order components. A combination of optical filters is used to select the required comb line. First, a conventional bandpass filter with a bandwidth of approximately 10 GHz isolates the spectral region containing the desired component, after which a narrowband dual cavity Bragg grating ring resonator (BGRR) with a bandwidth of approximately 3 MHz provides the final line selection. The selected comb line is then combined with an optical reference derived from the same laser and photodetected to generate the desired millimeter-wave or sub-terahertz signal through optical heterodyning. Numerical simulations are presented for 183- and 229-GHz generation, demonstrating the ability of the same underlying architecture to address multiple LO frequencies by tuning the OEO electrical filter to the appropriate oscillation frequency and selecting the corresponding comb order.

items.title_en: Spatiotemporal Imaging of Thermally Driven Metal-Insulator Phase Domain Propagation in VO2
items.title_zh: VO2中热驱动金属-绝缘体相畴传播的时空成像
items.abstract_en: Achieving a detailed picture of the nature and dynamics of phase boundaries remains a major challenge, particularly solid-solid transitions central to phase-change materials. Here, we use stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy and finite-element simulations to study the nonlinear thermally driven motion of the mesoscale insulator-metal phase boundary in VO2 thin films. We visualize the lateral spatiotemporal evolution of a diffraction-limited photoinduced metallic phase domain, resolving its outward propagation, contraction, and ultimate disappearance. The phase boundary dynamics are governed by heat flow, which can be controlled by excitation fluence, film thickness, and substrate thermal conductivity. Parameter-free agreement between the data and nonlinear thermal transport simulations identify the phase boundary transport as locally diffusive under this regime. We quantify how the latent heat acts as a thermal inertia, suppressing transport and prolonging the phase coexistence. Paradoxically, despite being driven by the underlying thermal gradient locally described by Fourier's law, the mesoscale phase front propagates faster than expected from thermal diffusion. This phenomenon arises from the distinction between temperature-field evolution and phase-boundary isotherm motion. These results establish a link between heat dissipation and mesoscale phase-front motion, providing a framework for controlling phase-transition kinetics relevant to photonics applications of VO2. We anticipate that this approach generalizes to a broad class of first- and second-order transitions.

items.title_en: High-order resonances and emergent coherent dynamics in interacting Stark chains
items.abstract_en: A linear potential gradient can strongly suppress quantum dynamics, while interactions can activate resonant many-body processes whose higher-order structure remains largely unexplored. Here we uncover a systematic hierarchy of high-order interaction--tilt resonances in an interacting Stark chain, where the resonance order counts the minimal number of elementary exchange steps involved. These resonances manifest as long-lived coherent oscillations with order-dependent timescales. By isolating individual resonant channels and developing a microscopic effective description, we connect these dynamical timescales to the underlying many-body exchange processes and reveal a pronounced dependence on the initial-state structure. Our results provide crucial insights into high-order many-body resonances and show how commensurate interaction-to-tilt ratios generate a hierarchy of parametrically slow coherent many-body dynamics.

items.title_en: Squeezing-type lower bounds on generalized metrological sensitivity
items.abstract_en: We introduce squeezing-type lower bounds for a hierarchy of variance bounds under specific unbiasedness constraints, which generalizes the quantum Cramér-Rao bound. Our construction directly extends standard squeezing coefficients to the corresponding generalized metrological sensitivities while retaining their experimentally accessible structure. We show how observables maximizing these bounds can be identified analytically within families of accessible observables. If arbitrary observables are accessible, the optimized squeezing-type bound recovers the exact generalized metrological sensitivity. These bounds provide efficient and experimentally viable characterizations of generalized metrological sensitivities that are especially relevant in finite-shot scenarios and in the transition from local to global parameter estimation.

items.title_en: Machine Learning-Assisted Discovery of Carbon-Related Defect Formation Mechanisms in Diamond
items.title_zh: 机器学习辅助发现金刚石中碳相关缺陷的形成机制
items.abstract_en: Diamond is an important host material for functional defects such as solid-state spin qubits. During the defect creation by irradiation and subsequent thermal annealing, carbon-related defects, including vacancies and interstitials, are generated and can migrate to form new defect complexes. To investigate this kinetically driven process and reveal the formation mechanisms of the di-interstitials and di-vacancies in the neutral charge state, we fine-tuned a universal machine learning interatomic potential using a small dataset generated from density functional theory calculations. We obtained a barrier of 1.84 eV for mono-interstitial migration and found that two initially separated mono-interstitials only need to overcome a lower barrier to form di-interstitial configurations. Beyond the training data, the MLIP also identified the formation pathway for an additional di-interstitial configuration and a stepwise divacancy dissociation mechanism. These results reveal migration-assisted defect complex formation mechanisms and demonstrate how targeted MLIP training can identify reaction pathways.

items.title_en: Optical vortex bullets with large angular momenta
items.abstract_en: We investigate three-dimensional spatiotemporal optical vortex solitons (light bullets with a toroidal shape) carrying higher-order orbital angular momentum in Kerr media with anomalous group-velocity dispersion and a transversely localized Gaussian profile of the linear refractive index. Stationary vortex bullets with topological charges (winding numbers) $1\leq \ell \leq 4$ are obtained as numerical solutions of the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and their existence, structure and stability are systematically analyzed. In terms of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates, these solutions represent matter-wave solitons with embedded vorticity. We examine the dependence of the solution families on the propagation constant, the depth and width of the guiding profile, and $\ell $. It is found that the increase of $\ell $ requires one to use a stronger or wider waveguiding potential to sustain localized states satisfying the Vakhitov-Kolokolov (VK) stability criterion. VK-complying and non-complying branches of vortex-soliton families are separated by a degenerate Townes branch. Direct simulations reveal that, although the guiding profile substantially suppresses the collapse and extends the propagation distance of vortex bullets, their robustness is ultimately limited by azimuthal instabilities, whose growth is enhanced for values of $\ell $. These results demonstrate that engineered refractive-index landscapes significantly enlarge the stability domain of spatiotemporal vortex bullets and provide guidelines for supporting optical bullets carrying large orbital angular momenta.

items.title_en: Study of non-uniformity-induced structured spectrum in a tapered optical fiber through stimulated four-wave mixing
items.abstract_en: Tapered optical fibers offer tunable dispersion and a small mode area, yielding high nonlinearity, which makes them ideal for nonlinear and quantum optics. Because phase-matched four-wave mixing strongly depends on dispersion, the taper diameter becomes a key parameter. For sub-micrometer tapers, identifying the exact diameter is challenging. Here, we show that when seeding with a broad spectrum, stimulated four-wave mixing yields a comb-like spectrum that is directly linked to the overall taper profile opening possibility for non-destructive evaluation of sub-micron taper. Our model based on joint-spectral amplitude includes the phase accumulated over the fiber length.

items.title_en: Physics-anchored residual quantum neural networks for cloud-cover parameterization
items.title_zh: 用于云量参数化的物理锚定残差量子神经网络
items.abstract_en: Compact quantum neural networks have been explored for cloud-cover parameterization, but their predictive value depends on how physical knowledge is incorporated and which classical models provide the reference. We investigate an offline residual formulation that retains a fitted \XR\ cloud-cover estimate and learns a correction to its logit in transformed target space. Using released ICON/DYAMOND-derived data, we compare ten model variants in six- and eight-input settings, with three matched replicates and 10,000 training samples per replicate. All quantum circuits use local Z readout and noiseless exact expectation values. Under a common 30-epoch protocol, residual prediction reduced physical-space test mean squared error relative to direct QNN prediction by 54.3\% and 38.8\% for six-input XYZ and ZZXY circuits, and by 49.2\% and 38.9\% for their eight-input versions. Residual QNNs also outperformed the selected compact residual multilayer perceptron in every paired replicate. A larger, longer-trained Grundner-Q1 adaptation nevertheless achieved lower error: residual Q1 reached mean MSEs of 0.00778 and 0.00791, compared with 0.01124 and 0.01082 for residual XYZ. The results support residual prediction for compact simulated QNNs within the tested budget and establish a clear boundary set by stronger classical references. They do not establish computational quantum advantage or online climate-model skill.

items.title_en: Finite-size scaling of spin-wave scattering and enhancement in magnonic Fabry-Pérot nanoresonators
items.title_zh: 磁振子法布里-珀罗纳米谐振器中自旋波散射与增强的有限尺寸标度
items.abstract_en: Magnonic neural networks require compact resonant nodes that scatter spin waves efficiently, concentrate spin-wave energy and can be reconfigured. Hybrid magnonic Fabry-Pérot resonators, formed by a ferromagnetic-metal stripe dipolar-coupled to a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) film, provide low-loss and programmable control of spin-wave transmission, but have so far been studied only for stripes that are long compared with the spin-wave wavelength. Here we use micromagnetic simulations to determine how the response of a 200-nm-wide CoFeB stripe on a 55-nm-thick YIG film evolves as the stripe length is reduced from infinity to 640 nm. An infinitely long stripe acts as a one-dimensional cavity that opens a transmission gap at the first-order resonance (1.70 GHz and 1.47 GHz for the parallel and antiparallel magnetic configuration) and enhances the out-of-plane precession amplitude in the YIG film by factors of about 5 and 12, without distorting the transmitted wavefront. For lengths of a few micrometers, backward-volume spin waves emitted from the stripe ends modulate the precession along the stripe and fragment the reflected and transmitted wavefronts. Below about 1.2 micrometer, the resonator scatters incident spin waves over the entire isofrequency contour of the film, with caustic beams that are most pronounced in the antiparallel configuration. In this regime the parallel configuration supports weakly enhanced quantized modes, whereas the antiparallel configuration supports a single mode with an out-of-plane enhancement of about 15. The width, thickness and shape of the stripe tune this mode by 50-100 MHz, and its strong enhancement lowers the onset of nonlinear frequency shift and fold-over to incident amplitudes of a few percent of the saturation magnetization. Sub-micrometer magnonic resonators are therefore promising reconfigurable nonlinear nodes for magnonic networks.

items.title_en: How Memristors Work: A Step-by-Step Guide to the CALM Model
items.title_zh: 忆阻器如何工作：CALM模型分步指南
items.abstract_en: Memristors made of very different materials, halide perovskites, metal oxides and nanofluidic channels, show a common set of dynamical features: two limiting conductances, hysteresis that depends on the scan rate, regular and inverted hysteresis loops, large and negative capacitances and inductive loops in impedance spectra, and potentiation and depression under pulse trains. This tutorial shows how a single minimal model, the conductance-activated quasi-linear memristor (CALM) model, explains all these features with three ingredients: the two conductance states, the rectification function x_eq (u) and the characteristic time tau(u). The tutorial is a slide presentation that the reader can follow alone, with exercises designed to be solved with the help of an AI assistant, reference Python code, and this support text. The text can also be read on its own: Section 4 gives a compact account of the content of the slides, with the main equations and figures, and the solutions to the exercises are given at the end.

items.title_en: Universal Quantum Criticality from a Gaussian Variational Manifold
items.abstract_en: Universal behavior at continuous phase transitions is encoded in long-wavelength fixed-point theories controlled by dimensionality and symmetries. It is a central question for which systems this universal behavior and the underlying long-wavelength description can be captured by a noninteracting theory allowing for analytical and accurate predictions. In this work we provide a systematic procedure for obtaining the best noninteracting fermionic description of a quantum phase transition through fermionic Gaussian states. We demonstrate the performance of our procedure for the interacting long-range transverse-field Ising chain. This formulation reduces the problem to a self-consistent Euler equation that yields a critical line in close agreement with independent numerical benchmarks, while its singular momentum structure provides analytic predictions for continuously varying critical properties. Yet exact diagonalization shows that Gaussian-state fidelity to the exact ground state is poorest, and non-Gaussianity strongest, near the transition. Thus, accurate predictions for critical properties can emerge from the Gaussian variational description even where its microscopic wave-function approximation is weakest.

items.title_en: Q-MALDetect: Quantum Image-Based Malware Detection and Adversarial Robustness Analysis
items.abstract_en: Quantum machine-learning (QML) models are increasingly considered for security applications, yet their adversarial robustness in malware analysis remains insufficiently understood. This paper presents Q-MALDetect, a hybrid convolutional and variational-quantum detector for byte-image representations of x86-64 Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) binaries, and evaluates it under feature-space and a range of Grad-CAM-guided, executable-aware evasion attacks. The model achieves 97.2% training accuracy, but its robustness deteriorates as attack strength increases, with the strongest evaluated feature-space attack reaching a 78.7% attack success rate (ASR). Among executable-aware attacks, Grad-CAM-guided no-operation (NOP) insertion produces the highest conditional ASR of 32.9%. Dynamic adversarial training is the most effective evaluated defense, reducing feature-space ASR to as low as 5.0%, executable-aware ASR to 7.7%, and the sequential-attack ASR to 34.0%. In contrast, convolutional-autoencoder preprocessing increases executable-aware ASR to 39.7%, coinciding with a rise in Grad-CAM attribution mass within the mutable .text region from 35.2% to 45.7%. Ablation results reveal no monotonic relationship between qubit count and robustness, while the encoding interface modifies the learned attack surface without neutralizing the strongest attack. These findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of attacks and defenses depends strongly on the perturbation constraints and evaluation conditions. Reliable deployment of QML malware detectors therefore requires assessment against both feature-space and executable-aware attacks rather than reliance on clean accuracy or generic denoising alone.

items.title_en: Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Transitions on a Quantum Processor
items.abstract_en: Mixed quantum states can exhibit unconventional forms of symmetry breaking without pure-state counterparts. A prominent example is strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB), which cannot be diagnosed by observables linear in the density matrix. Here, we experimentally resolve finite-size critical signatures of SW-SSB transitions on a superconducting quantum processor. We develop a measurement protocol that combines quantum measurements with classical processing based on the known dephasing channel to reconstruct nonlinear mixed-state correlators. Using only two measurement settings, the protocol reconstructs fidelity, Rényi-2, and linear correlators, as well as string observables. Applying this approach to matrix-product states subjected to power-law-correlated dephasing, we observe finite-size crossings and scaling collapses in nonlinear correlators, accompanied by decaying linear correlations. We further map the estimated SW-SSB transition points across initial-state and channel parameters. Measurements of linear and Rényi-2 string observables further reveal signatures of mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases, with a nonlinear string-order crossover aligned with an independently estimated SW-SSB transition point. Our results establish a quantum-classical approach to probing SW-SSB critical behavior and mixed-state SPT order.

items.title_en: The Fundamental Memory Ceiling of Noisy Quantum Reservoirs
items.abstract_en: Fresh qubits, not size, set how long a noisy quantum system can remember. With $k$ input qubits reinitialized per time step, the longest memory any reservoir can attain under depolarizing noise is $\exp[Θ(k)]$ time steps, whatever its size, dynamics, and input encoding. A universal upper bound and an explicit reservoir that attains the exponential scaling establish this optimal resource law. The bound depends on the dynamics only through the entropy that fresh qubits remove per time step, so it holds for any Markovian noisy dynamics without feedback, including measurement-free error correction.

items.title_en: Sidewall Metrology Protocol for Superconducting Qubit Devices
items.abstract_en: Sidewall morphology is a potentially important factor influencing superconducting qubit performance, yet its quantitative characterization remains challenging due to the absence of standardized measurement protocols. In this work, we develop a scanning probe microscopy-based measurement framework for the quantitative characterization of superconducting qubit sidewalls. The framework introduces a refined root mean square lateral sidewall roughness descriptor and a new curvature-equivalent radius for quantifying vertical sidewall morphology. The descriptors and measurement procedures are applied to different components of qubit devices, forming the basis of a proposed sidewall characterization protocol. This provides a foundation for quantitative comparisons of fabrication processes across laboratories, enabling future investigations of correlations between sidewall geometry and qubit performance.

items.title_en: A Readout-Aware Theory of Approximate Heisenberg Propagation
items.abstract_en: Classical methods for computing quantum expectation values often propagate observables in the Heisenberg picture. To remain tractable, these methods rely on approximations that discard operator components during evolution. Yet the magnitude of these components alone does not determine the resulting expectation-value error, which also depends on their subsequent evolution and the input state. We develop \emph{generalized Pauli propagation}, a common algebraic framework encompassing Pauli propagation, Lie-algebraic simulation, and Krylov subspace methods. Using weighted commutator graphs, we derive exact identities that relate approximation errors to the signed contributions of omitted and discarded operator components. Our central result establishes \emph{delayed observability}, identifying conditions under which these contributions vanish at low orders in propagation time. We use this structure to develop finite-order error estimates and state-dependent selection rules. We further prove that retaining the symmetry-preserving part of a weak perturbation eliminates first-order expectation-value errors under suitable symmetry conditions. By revealing how approximation errors affect the desired expectation value, our framework provides a basis for more informative error analysis and the development of readout-aware simulation strategies.

items.title_en: Wave-Particle Complementarity in Quantum Walk from a Quantum Mechanical Perspective
items.abstract_en: A quantum walk is a mathematical model and a quantum version of a random walk. For the past two decades, it has been studied from mathematical and physical viewpoints. It has many desirable properties. This paper reevaluates quantum walk from a quantum mechanical perspective, as Feynman essentially proposed it as a toy model in his path integral method. Then we demonstrate that the quantum walk model exhibits both particle-like and wave-like properties by showing reflection and partial reflection as a particle and interference as a wave. In particular, for an initial state supported at two sites $\pm\ell$, we explicitly derive the weak limit distribution of the Hadamard walk and show that the Konno distribution is modulated by the interference factor $2\cos^2(\ell k(x))$. The resulting interference profile is reminiscent of far-field (Fraunhofer-type) diffraction.

items.title_en: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
items.title_zh: 将参数高效微调扩展到脑编码任务
items.abstract_en: Brain encoding models aim to predict neural responses to stimuli. The most widely used approach fits readouts from frozen pretrained backbones. Using neural data to train large models from scratch or fully fine-tune them after task-pretraining has proven difficult because neural data is costly and limited. We show that parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) enables us to effectively adapt very large pretrained backbones for brain encoding with a small number of trainable parameters. To make it computationally practical, we exploit the backbone's causal structure to predict multiple timepoints in a single pass instead of using sliding windows, significantly reducing feature-extraction cost. This enables efficient fine-tuning of multimodal backbones with up to 104B parameters, the largest model adapted for brain encoding to our knowledge. Trained with a low-rank adapter (LoRA) and a lightweight readout, our approach consistently improves brain encoding performance across nine diverse multimodal backbones. On the same Qwen3-Omni backbone as the prior state-of-the-art (SoTA), our method BrainLoRA achieves the best published performance on the Algonauts 2025 Challenge. We also show the adapted multimodal backbones remain interpretable: modality attribution recovers the canonical sensory topography that prior work often obtains by construction from separate unimodal encoders, and neural adaptation increases the contribution of audio inputs and cross-modal mixing within the backbone. To scale out the number of adapted models, we develop a multi-LoRA kernel that accelerates joint training of multiple LoRAs on a shared backbone. This enables an ensemble of 200+ adapted models that ranks first on the public Algonauts post-challenge leaderboard at the time of writing. Together, our results highlight PEFT as an efficient and powerful paradigm for brain encoding.
items.abstract_zh: 脑编码模型旨在预测大脑对刺激的神经响应，主流做法是在冻结的预训练骨干上拟合读出层；由于神经数据昂贵且有限，从头训练或全量微调大模型十分困难。本文表明参数高效微调（PEFT）可用少量可训练参数有效适配超大预训练骨干。为降低计算量，作者利用骨干的因果结构一次预测多个时间点以替代滑动窗口，显著减少特征提取开销，从而可高效微调多达 104B 参数的多模态骨干（据称是用于脑编码的最大模型）。方法采用 LoRA 与轻量读出层，在九种多模态骨干上一致提升性能，并在 Algonauts 2025 挑战赛上取得最佳公开成绩。
items.highlight_zh: LoRA 微调千亿级多模态骨干，刷新脑编码基准
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：脑编码模型要预测大脑对图像、声音等刺激的神经响应。主流做法是用一个冻结的预训练大模型（视觉或语言骨干）抽取特征，再在其上拟合读出层。问题在于：神经数据（如 fMRI）昂贵、被试少、样本有限，因此要微调大模型很困难，从头训练也不现实。
方法：作者引入参数高效微调（PEFT），用极少量可训练参数去适配超大预训练骨干。为了让计算上可行，他们利用骨干网络的因果结构，一次前向就预测多个时间点，而不是用滑动窗口逐个预测，大幅降低特征提取成本，从而可以微调多达 104B 参数的多模态骨干（作者称这是目前用于脑编码的最大模型）。具体用 LoRA 低秩适配器加轻量读出层。
结果：在九种不同的多模态骨干上，该方法都稳定提升脑编码性能；在与此前最优方法相同的 Qwen3-Omni 骨干上，BrainLoRA 取得 Algonauts 2025 挑战赛已发表的最好成绩。可解释性方面也有发现：用模态归因可以恢复出经典的感官地形图，而这一结果此前往往要靠分别训练单模态编码器人为构造出来；神经适配还提高了音频输入的贡献以及骨干内部的跨模态混合。此外，作者开发了 multi-LoRA 内核，加速在共享骨干上联合训练多个 LoRA，从而可以训练 200 多个适配模型的集成，并在公开的 post-challenge 排行榜上排名第一。
为何重要：它说明“少改参数、多用大模型”的思路同样适用于神经数据稀缺的脑编码任务，把模型规模推到前所未有的量级，同时保持可解释性与工程可扩展性。

items.title_en: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
items.title_zh: MemT-1.0：迈向记忆原生演化
items.abstract_en: Memory-native evolution requires making memory an intrinsic capability of foundation models, enabling them to continuously accumulate and utilize information. To this end, we introduce MemT-1.0, a new architecture of memory foundation models that internalize memory as part of model computation. Building on Metis, MemT-1.0 employs Gated DeltaNet-2 with a stable token-level memory update mechanism within each turn. We further introduce Mixture-of-Storage to scale native memory capacity. Following a deliberate backbone preparation, we develop a two-stage training pipeline consisting of continued pre-training and post-training, supported by 34B tokens of training data and efficient training and inference infrastructure. We release a model family comprising MemT-1.0-Nano and MemT-1.0-Flash, and conduct a comprehensive evaluation of memory and general capabilities. The results show that they outperform the parametric memory baselines on average and remain competitive with retrieval-augmented methods, while largely preserving general capabilities. At a history length of 128K tokens, MemT-1.0-Nano achieves approximately $1.86\times$ end-to-end inference speedup and a $66\times$ reduction in persistent storage relative to full context KV cache. By internalizing retrieved procedural experience, MemT-1.0 improves task success on agentic tasks, providing a practical step toward memory-native evolution.
items.abstract_zh: 记忆原生演化要求把记忆内化为基础模型的内在能力，使其能够持续积累和利用信息。为此，作者提出记忆基础模型新架构 MemT-1.0，把记忆作为模型计算的一部分。它在 Metis 基础上采用 Gated DeltaNet-2，在每一轮内实现稳定的 token 级记忆更新，并引入 Mixture-of-Storage 扩展原生记忆容量。经过主干准备与两阶段训练（继续预训练与后训练），使用 34B token 数据与高效的训练推理设施，发布 MemT-1.0-Nano 与 MemT-1.0-Flash。评测显示，二者在记忆任务上平均优于参数化记忆基线，与检索增强方法相当，且基本保留通用能力；历史长度 128K 时，Nano 端到端推理提速约 1.86 倍，持久存储相比全上下文 KV cache 减少 66 倍；通过内化检索到的程序性经验，智能体任务成功率也得到提升。
items.highlight_zh: 将记忆内化为模型计算：128K 上下文推理提速 1.86 倍、存储省 66 倍
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】大模型的“记忆”通常靠把历史塞进上下文窗口或外挂检索库，模型本身并不会真正“记住”。论文追问：能否把记忆做成模型计算的一部分，让它像人一样持续积累经验？
【用了什么方法】提出 MemT-1.0 架构：在 Metis 基础上用 Gated DeltaNet-2 做 token 级记忆更新，保证每轮写入稳定；再用 Mixture-of-Storage 扩大原生记忆容量。训练分两阶段——继续预训练加后训练，共 34B token，并配套高效训练与推理基础设施。发布 Nano 与 Flash 两个尺寸。
【有什么结果】在记忆类评测上平均优于参数化记忆基线，与检索增强方法基本打平，同时通用能力没有明显下降。历史长度 128K 时，Nano 端到端推理快约 1.86 倍，持久存储比全上下文 KV cache 少 66 倍。在智能体任务中，把检索到的程序性经验内化进模型后，成功率上升。
【为何重要】它把长上下文的代价从推理时的显存/存储转移到参数化记忆上，是通向“记忆原生”模型的一次实际探索，对长对话、智能体与持续学习都有参考价值。

items.title_en: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
items.title_zh: 面向长上下文线性注意力的 Kronecker Delta 规则
items.abstract_en: We propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, a novel update rule for associative matrix memories. KronLSTM extends the xLSTM family with a memory-revision mechanism that corrects targeted associations while modifying the memory only along a single direction in matrix space. This minimally invasive memory revision reduces interference with previously stored information compared with delta-rule updates, making it particularly well suited for long-context language modeling. The resulting memory dynamics can be mathematically described as a Markov chain that converges to a steady-state distribution, while the expected norm of the memory matrix remains uniformly bounded throughout the entire input sequence. Hence, KronLSTM ensures stable memory dynamics without requiring additional normalization and stabilization mechanisms for the memory state. Experiments show that KronLSTM is competitive with, and often outperforms, existing linear attention architectures, including models of the (Gated) DeltaNet family, with particularly strong performance on long context benchmarks. These results establish the Kronecker Delta Rule as an effective and analytically tractable foundation for stable associative memory in recurrent linear attention architectures. Our code (https://github.com/NX-AI/KronLSTM) and models (https://huggingface.co/collections/NX-AI/kronlstm) are open-source.
items.abstract_zh: 本文提出 KronLSTM，一种基于 Kronecker Delta 规则的线性注意力架构；该规则是针对联想矩阵记忆的新更新规则。KronLSTM 扩展 xLSTM 家族，引入记忆修正机制：既能纠正目标关联，又只沿矩阵空间中的单一方向修改记忆。与 delta 规则相比，这种微创式修正减少了对已存信息的干扰，因而特别适合长上下文语言建模。其记忆动态可被描述为收敛到稳态分布的马尔可夫链，记忆矩阵的期望范数在整条输入序列上始终有界，因此无需额外的归一化与稳定化机制。实验显示其与现有线性注意力架构（包括 (Gated) DeltaNet 家族）相当甚至往往更优，在长上下文基准上尤其突出。代码与模型已开源。
items.highlight_zh: Kronecker Delta 规则实现微创记忆修正，长上下文更强且动态稳定
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】线性注意力用固定大小的矩阵记忆压缩历史，但如何写入新信息而不擦掉旧的，一直是难题。经典的 delta 规则每次用新键值对“覆盖”某个方向，容易干扰已存内容。
【用了什么方法】作者提出 Kronecker Delta Rule 更新规则与 KronLSTM 架构，扩展 xLSTM 家族。关键点是“微创修正”：只沿矩阵空间中的单一方向修改记忆，在纠正目标关联的同时尽量不动其他关联。他们还给出理论分析：记忆动态是可收敛到稳态分布的马尔可夫链，记忆矩阵的期望范数在整条序列上一致有界，因此不需要额外的归一化或稳定化技巧。
【有什么结果】与 (Gated) DeltaNet 等现有线性注意力架构相比有竞争力，且常常更优，长上下文基准上优势尤其明显。
【为何重要】它为循环式线性注意力提供了一种既有效又可解析分析的稳定联想记忆基础，说明长上下文建模不必只靠“越大越贵”的 KV 缓存。代码与模型均已开源，便于复现与后续研究。

items.title_en: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
items.title_zh: 基于神经算子的噪声下规划
items.abstract_en: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. Building on an established screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control, we address two challenges: specifying boundary conditions that support navigation across varying geometries and efficiently computing fields with reliable gradients. Zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries terminate sampled paths at walls, weakening the goal signal along long routes and making it harder to estimate reliably. We instead impose reflecting Neumann conditions on obstacles and a Dirichlet condition at the goal, allowing sampled paths to continue exploring free space until they reach the target. To solve the resulting PDE without a configuration-space mesh, we extend a Monte Carlo (MC) solver, Walk on Stars (WoSt), to higher dimensions. However, local MC fluctuations can reverse estimated gradient directions and cause planning failures, making direct planning require costly sampling. PUN amortizes this computation by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example. At inference, test-time scaling uses bounded local search guided by the predicted global field. We evaluate PUN on planning tasks across dimensions. Across four noise levels, PUN matches or outperforms all compared planners, achieving 95-100% success on the 4D replanning benchmark while maintaining the lowest runtime. At the highest tested noise level in 4D, PUN achieves 10.7-60.6% relative gains in success rate over other methods while running 3.29-32.15 times faster.
items.abstract_zh: 在控制执行存在不确定噪声时进行规划，需要能在多样环境中可靠工作的反馈策略。我们提出 Planning Under Noise（PUN），一种学习噪声感知价值场的神经算子，可在未见过的几何环境中用于规划。基于随机最优控制中已有的 screened-Poisson 表述，我们解决两个挑战：指定支持跨不同几何导航的边界条件，以及高效计算具有可靠梯度的场。零 Dirichlet 障碍边界会在墙壁处终止采样路径，削弱长路径上的目标信号并使其更难可靠估计。我们改为在障碍上施加反射 Neumann 条件、在目标处施加 Dirichlet 条件，使采样路径能继续探索自由空间直至到达目标。为在无需构型空间网格的情况下求解所得 PDE，我们将蒙特卡洛（MC）求解器 Walk on Stars（WoSt）推广到更高维。然而局部 MC 涨落可能反转估计的梯度方向、导致规划失败，使直接规划需要昂贵的采样。PUN 通过从含噪、部分收敛的蒙特卡洛标签中学习几何到场映射来摊销这一计算，避免为每个训练样本付出昂贵的收敛代价。推理时，测试时扩展使用由预测全局场引导的有界局部搜索。我们在跨维度的规划任务上评估 PUN：在四个噪声水平下，PUN 匹敌或优于所有对比规划器，在 4D 重规划基准上达到 95-100% 成功率，同时保持最低运行时间；在 4D 最高测试噪声水平下，PUN 相比其他方法取得 10.7-60.6% 的成功率相对提升，且运行速度快 3.29-32.15 倍。
items.highlight_zh: PUN 学噪声感知价值场，4D 重规划成功率 95-100% 且更快
items.digest_zh:
研究了什么问题：机器人在执行动作时难免受噪声干扰，需要在没见过的环境里也能可靠地规划路径。核心难题是如何学到一个“知道噪声在哪、该往哪走”的价值场，并且算得足够快。

用了什么方法：沿用随机最优控制的 screened-Poisson 表述，把规划化成求解一个偏微分方程。两个关键改动：一是障碍物边界改用反射 Neumann 条件、只在目标点用 Dirichlet 条件，避免采样路径一碰墙就终止、导致长路径上目标信号太弱；二是把蒙特卡洛 PDE 求解器 Walk on Stars 推广到高维，从而无需构建构型空间网格。由于 MC 采样有涨落、会翻转梯度方向并造成规划失败，作者训练神经算子 PUN，从“含噪、未完全收敛”的 MC 标签中直接学习“几何→价值场”的映射，把昂贵求解摊销掉；推理时再用预测的全局场引导有界局部搜索，实现测试时扩展。

有什么结果：在多个维度的规划任务上，PUN 在四种噪声水平下均匹敌或优于对比方法；4D 重规划基准成功率达 95-100%，运行时间最低；在 4D 最高噪声下，成功率相对提升 10.7-60.6%，速度快 3.29-32.15 倍。

为何重要：说明把执行噪声显式建模进价值场、并用神经算子摊销昂贵的 PDE 求解，可以在高维、强噪声条件下实现既快又稳的规划，为真实机器人部署提供可行路径。

items.title_en: Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction: How far should we go?
items.title_zh: 自适应多token预测：我们该推测多远？
items.abstract_en: Multi-token prediction (MTP) can accelerate language-model decoding by drafting several tokens and verifying them in a single target-model pass. However, the best speculation horizon changes with context: longer drafts offer greater amortization when reliable, but can waste compute on suffixes discarded after a rejection. Unlike autoregressive drafting, where a stopping rule can decide token by token, MTP must fix the horizon before drafting, as all heads fire in the same forward pass. We therefore formulate horizon selection as an online control problem, using verification feedback to learn how far the draft can be trusted in each context, and introduce Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction (AMTP): a lightweight controller that requires no retraining and leaves the exact verifier unchanged. To guide horizon selection, we characterize the expected number of tokens committed at each horizon via acceptance survival, the probability that a draft prefix is fully accepted. Before each round, AMTP predicts how far the draft is likely to survive and picks the horizon with the highest expected tokens per second, learning freely from every verification pass. Theoretically, we show that any online learner's prediction error translates into throughput regret against the best horizon for each context, and in turn into a bound on wall-clock completion time. With online gradient descent, this regret is sublinear. Across five draft-target pairings built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with Medusa heads, Meta's MTP models, and Qwen3-4B-Inst-2507-MTP, evaluated on AIME 2025 and GSM8K, AMTP decodes up to 4.1x faster than standard decoding and matches or outperforms the fixed window in 8 of 10 settings, with throughput gains of up to 10%.
items.abstract_zh: 多token预测（MTP）一次起草多个token，再由目标模型单次前向统一验证以加速解码，但最优推测长度会随上下文变化：草稿较长时若可靠则收益更大，一旦被拒绝，剩余部分又会浪费算力。与可逐token停止的自回归起草不同，MTP必须在起草前固定长度。作者把长度选择建模为在线控制问题，提出无需重训练、不改变精确验证器的轻量控制器AMTP：它以“接受存活率”（草稿前缀被完整接受的概率）预测草稿能存活多深，并选择期望吞吐最高的长度，且能从每次验证中持续学习。理论上证明预测误差可转化为吞吐遗憾并约束完成时间，在线梯度下降下达次线性。在五组草稿-目标配对、AIME 2025与GSM8K上，AMTP最高比标准解码快4.1倍，10个设置中8个不劣于固定窗口。
items.highlight_zh: 免重训练自适应推测长度，解码最高提速4.1倍
items.digest_zh:
① 要解决的问题：大模型逐token解码慢。多token预测（MTP）让模型一次“打草稿”多个token，再由原模型一次前向统一验证，接受正确前缀，丢掉后面的错误token。但起草多长才合适？上下文简单时草稿越长越划算，上下文困难时草稿越长越浪费算力。
② 难点：自回归起草能逐token判断何时停；MTP的多个预测头在同一次前向中同时输出，必须在起草前一次性定好长度，事后无法反悔。
③ 方法：把“每轮该走多远”当作在线控制问题。核心量是“接受存活率”，即草稿前k个token被全部接受的概率；据此估出各个长度的期望提交token数，再用耗时折算成每秒token数，选吞吐最高的长度。控制器很轻，不改模型、不重训练，也不改动精确验证器，因此输出分布不变。每轮验证的真实结果都当作反馈，用在线梯度下降更新预测。
④ 理论保证：预测越准，吞吐遗憾越小；遗憾又被转化为实际完成时间的上界，且用在线梯度下降时遗憾次线性增长，即越用越准。
⑤ 结果：在Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct配Medusa头、Meta的MTP模型、Qwen3-4B-Inst-2507-MTP构成的五组配对上，于AIME 2025和GSM8K评测，最高比标准解码快4.1倍；10个设置中有8个持平或超过最佳固定窗口，吞吐最多再提升10%。
⑥ 意义：说明推测解码里“草稿多长”这个关键超参数可以随上下文自适应，而且几乎零额外训练成本，是一条实用的加速路径。

items.title_en: Efficient Edge-aware Attention Network for Graph Generation
items.title_zh: 面向图生成的高效边感知注意力网络
items.abstract_en: Graph generative models commonly use graph-specific Transformer architectures to jointly update node and edge features. However, these architectures do not directly benefit from recent hardware-aware attention implementations, limiting their scalability. The adaptation is, however, non-trivial: edge and graph-level features must be injected into pairwise attention scores, graph masks must be respected, and dynamic edge updates remain a major source of quadratic memory usage. We propose an edge-aware attention layer for graph generation that incorporates structural information through head-wise score modulation, while updating edge representations with a lightweight residual mechanism that retains attention-score dependent edge updates. This layer can be effectively implemented using PyTorch's FlexAttention. We achieve similar generation quality to our baseline while reducing peak GPU memory by around 65% and substantially improving training and sampling throughput. These results suggest that the proposed architecture is a practical step toward scalable graph foundation models.
items.abstract_zh: 图生成模型常用图专用的Transformer架构联合更新节点与边特征，但难以直接受益于近期的硬件友好型注意力实现，限制了可扩展性。适配并不简单：边与图级特征需注入成对注意力分数，必须遵守图掩码，动态边更新仍是二次内存占用的主要来源。作者提出一种用于图生成的边感知注意力层，通过逐头分数调制注入结构信息，并用轻量残差机制更新边表示，同时保留依赖注意力分数的边更新。该层可用PyTorch的FlexAttention高效实现。在生成质量与基线相当的同时，峰值GPU显存降低约65%，训练与采样吞吐显著提升，表明该架构是迈向可扩展图基础模型的务实一步。
items.highlight_zh: 边感知注意力层借FlexAttention实现，显存降约65%
items.digest_zh:
① 研究问题：图生成模型（例如用图Transformer在每一层同时更新节点特征和边特征）生成质量好，但训练和采样都很慢、显存吃紧，原因之一是它们用不了FlashAttention、FlexAttention这类针对GPU硬件优化的高效注意力实现。
② 为什么不能直接换：结构信息（边特征、图级特征）需要加进成对的注意力分数里；还必须遵守图的掩码规则；而且每层都要动态更新边表示，这部分是二次内存开销的大头。现成的高效注意力接口并不支持这些操作。
③ 方法：作者设计了一个边感知注意力层——用“逐头分数调制”把结构和边信息注入各注意力头的打分；边表示则用轻量残差方式更新，同时保留“边更新依赖注意力分数”这一关键性质。整个层能直接映射到PyTorch的FlexAttention上运行，从而吃到硬件加速。
④ 结果：生成质量与原来的基线相当，但峰值GPU显存降低约65%，训练和采样速度大幅提升。
⑤ 意义：把图生成模型从“自己写的慢注意力”迁到通用高效注意力内核上，使更大规模、更高分辨率的图生成成为可能，是走向图基础模型的一步实用工程与架构改进。

items.title_en: Turning TS2Vec into a Foundation Model for Time Series Classification
items.title_zh: 将TS2Vec转变为用于时间序列分类的基础模型
items.abstract_en: TS2Vec is one of the strongest self-supervised methods for time series classification, introduced in 2022. It is designed to be trained anew on every dataset: self-supervised pre-training followed by linear probing. Since then, the field has shifted towards foundation models that reuse one encoder across datasets. Yet TS2Vec offers a compact convolutional architecture that operates directly on temporal samples and accepts variable-length inputs without resampling. We ask whether these properties can be retained when the encoder is pre-trained only once, and show that they can: TS2Vec can essentially be turned into a foundation model. Three changes suffice: pre-train on a synthetic corpus, feed the encoder a raw amplitude view and an instance-normalized shape view of the input through two small stems, and distill one specialist encoder per view into a single encoder. The result, TS2Vec-FM, is a 1.6M-parameter dilated convolutional network that, kept frozen, reaches 83.3% on UCR-128 and 75.3% on UEA-27 under linear probing, within 0.3 pp of MantisV2, the current state of the art, and above TS2Vec trained separately on each target dataset. What we find most interesting is how different TS2Vec-FM is from other foundation models in design: near-parity is reached without attention, without a patch tokenizer, and without intermediate-layer extraction, using an "old-school" convolutional encoder and a two-layer MLP stem.

items.title_en: PaPi: Parallel Picard-Duhamel Integration for Fast Neuro-Spectral Architectures
items.title_zh: PaPi：面向快速神经谱架构的并行Picard-Duhamel积分
items.abstract_en: Neuro-spectral architectures (NeuSA) are a class of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that have proven effective for solving time-dependent PDEs in the frequency domain. However, training and inference often rely on costly numerical integration of the learned vector field, typically using sequential Runge-Kutta time stepping, which limits temporal parallelism. We introduce PaPi, an integration scheme inspired by weakly nonlinear flows that enables time-Parallel inference through exponential integration and a Duhamel-Picard scheme. We show that the Duhamel-Picard iteration converges exponentially for all flows, and provide explicit error bounds that depend on how close the flow is to linear. Experiments show that PaPi accelerates training and inference by up to two orders of magnitude, achieving training times of under one second for low-dimensional PDE learning problems, while maintaining competitive predictive accuracy.

items.title_en: Two $\operatorname{ReLU}$ Layers is All You Need
items.title_zh: 两层ReLU足矣
items.abstract_en: We prove that every $\operatorname{ReLU}$ network can be exactly simulated by a $\operatorname{ReLU}$ network with two hidden layers. We present two proofs: one that is based on fillings in homological algebra and a direct combinatorial proof.

items.title_en: Continuous-Time Policy Gradient from Discrete Data: Convergence Analysis and Model-Free Algorithms
items.title_zh: 离散数据下的连续时间策略梯度：收敛性分析与无模型算法
items.abstract_en: Continuous-time reinforcement learning seeks an optimal policy under unknown dynamics driven by stochastic differential equations using observations collected at discrete times. We develop a policy gradient framework that combines rigorous convergence analysis with learning from discrete data. We first establish a performance difference lemma and derive policy gradient formulas for randomized and parametrized policies. We then prove exponential convergence of an entropy-regularized policy flow to the regularized optimum. For discrete parametrized updates, we derive a convergence bound that explicitly separates the contributions of critic error, policy-regression error, and the learning step size. To enable learning under unknown dynamics, we integrate this framework with PhiBE, which constructs a continuous-time surrogate generator from discrete transition data. The resulting on-policy and off-policy model-free actor-critic algorithms preserve the continuous-time structure of the control problem. Numerical experiments on an entropy-regularized linear-quadratic regulator and a nonlinear wheeled robot demonstrate the performance and stability of the proposed methods with both known and data-driven dynamics.

items.title_en: The Token-Energy Law of LLM Decode: Active Bytes and Realized Time Account for Joules per Token
items.title_zh: LLM 解码的 Token-Energy 定律：活跃字节与实现时间解释每 Token 焦耳能耗
items.abstract_en: Energy-efficient deployment of large language models requires understanding how model architecture, hardware, and serving settings shape energy per generated token. We introduce the Token-Energy Law, a compact, interpretable model of GPU-board energy per output token for dense, full-history decoding. It relates token energy to two core dimensions: active bytes and realized decode time. Active bytes describe logical byte demand per output, separating dense weights shared within a decode iteration from private key--value (KV) histories read and updated for each request. Realized decode time is the elapsed decode duration divided by the number of output tokens produced. We combine the two byte coordinates and time in a common affine form, with coefficients calibrated for each model and hardware/runtime configuration. This formulation explains how batching amortizes shared-weight work, longer attended histories increase private KV demand, and throughput determines the time-associated cost per output. Our experiments cover three models under BF16 decoding on NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, including two-GPU tensor parallelism on Hopper. Using fixed coefficients and observed decode time, held-out condition-mean energy estimates differ from measurements by at most 3.73%.

items.title_en: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval
items.title_zh: 面向生成式检索的演化语义索引
items.abstract_en: Generative retrieval (GR) casts search and recommendation as autoregressive generation of discrete semantic identifiers (SIDs). SID design largely determines GR quality, but its discrete, interdependent components (SID construction, collision handling, decoding, and training) cannot be optimized end-to-end with gradients and remain largely hand-designed. We introduce a framework that improves these components through LLM-driven evolutionary program search, to our knowledge the first application of this approach to GR. A locally served, open-weight 31B model mutates executable GR components, so no proprietary LLM API is used, and a 1M-parameter proxy decoder provides fast feedback in place of repeatedly training the 1B target generator. Across 21 SID programs on NQ320K, proxy and target Recall@100 show strong rank correlation (Spearman $ρ= 0.90$). Guided by this proxy, evolution improves the seed GR on NQ320K, MSMARCO300K, and a multilingual e-commerce dataset under a fixed training recipe. On NQ320K, jointly evolving SID construction and collision handling improves Recall@1 from 55.8% to 59.3% and Recall@100 from 85.8% to 90.6%. A component study shows that proxy reliability depends on what is evolved: improvements transfer reliably for the semantic index but not for the generator's training objective or the full pipeline. LLM-driven evolutionary search is thus a practical tool for GR design, provided proxy reliability is established for the chosen search space.

items.title_en: The Dynamics of Collapse and Recovery in Clustered Federated Learning
items.title_zh: 聚类联邦学习中的崩溃与恢复动力学
items.abstract_en: Clustered federated learning (CFL) can suffer from cluster collapse. In particular, under unfavorable initialization, early client assignments concentrate heterogeneous groups on one cluster model, which is then trained toward a pooled compromise, while another model receives no updates. Since the current models determine client routing and routing determines subsequent model updates, we formulate clustered federated learning as control of an unknown dynamical system, with cluster models as the evolving state, client routing patterns as the control input, and routing interventions as state dependent controllers. In a two group linear model, we identify an initialization region in which greedy routing makes collapse self reinforcing. We then derive finite horizon error dynamics showing how routing interventions can reverse collapse by repeatedly training the starved model, primarily with updates from its compatible group. Motivated by this condition, each client uses blocked EXP3 to choose between greedy routing and interventions that redirect updates toward unused models. Experiments show that with simpler predictors and faster specialist formation, autonomous controller selection recovers usable specialists from unfavorable starts that trap standard CFL baselines. In transformed FEMNIST, the synchronized-entry configuration with persistent commitment recovers usable specialists in settings where the autonomous controller configuration often does not. Code and scripts for reproducing the experiments and figures are available at https://github.com/prsinha1/FedRecover.

items.title_en: Asymmetric Bidirectional Predictive Dynamics in Google Search and COVID-19 Time Series: A Multi-Horizon Forecast-Error Analysis
items.title_zh: Google 搜索与 COVID-19 时间序列中的非对称双向预测动力学：多时间跨度预测误差分析
items.abstract_en: Online search activity is widely used as a digital trace of information seeking during epidemics, but its predictive value is often reduced to correlation, a selected lag, or a single forecast-error score. We examine eight pre-specified Google Trends-COVID-19 pairs in both directions using matched LightGBM forecasts over rolling 400-day windows and horizons of 1-14 days. Log-RMSE gain is combined with forecast-error distribution entropy (FEDE), which captures horizon-dependent changes in the signed error distribution. The resulting directional predictive signature comprises response class, RMSE effect, FEDE endpoint and early-slope responses, persistence across rolling regimes, and horizon profile. For screening candidate directions, we also introduce a relative persistence-weighted directional predictive response strength (DPRS) on a within-study 0-100 scale; 100 denotes the strongest observed response in the comparison set, not an absolute coupling maximum. The pairs show concordant, RMSE-only, FEDE-only, and mixed responses. "loss of smell" -> reported cases is accuracy-dominant, with mean log-RMSE gain 0.104 (about 9.9% equivalent RMSE reduction) and DPRS 100, whereas the reverse direction is FEDE-dominant (D_FEDE=0.048; DPRS=42). "covid test" -> positive rate is FEDE-dominant (D_FEDE=0.039; positive in 72% of windows; DPRS=98) despite negative RMSE gain, while "lockdown" -> stringency is the clearest concordant case (DPRS=78). World-level symptom/case pairs are less persistent. Thus, forecast accuracy and error-distribution dynamics are complementary, predictive effects can be direction- and metric-dependent, and forecast horizon is part of the relationship. Aggregated regime-level patterns should not be extrapolated to individual time points or interpreted as evidence of causality.

items.title_en: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
items.title_zh: OptScientist：优化规律的自动发现
items.abstract_en: Many scientific phenomena are best understood as outcomes of underlying optimization problems, yet automated scientific discovery has largely focused on recovering equations that describe observed input-output patterns. We introduce OptScientist, a novel automated framework for discovering compact symbolic optimization laws directly from data. OptScientist comprises (i) a model that infers symbolic optimization problems by first learning to represent data as an optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form, and (ii) an LLM agentic system embedding the model in a discovery process that integrates theoretical priors from scientific literature, discovers candidate laws, abstracts their underlying mechanisms, and suggests new data to collect. We first evaluate OptScientist on OptFeynman, a novel benchmark of 99 physics-derived optimization problems, where OptScientist recovers ground-truth laws for over 80% of the problems and remains robust to noisy contextual information, while substantially outperforming machine-learning, symbolic, and LLM-based model-discovery baselines. On human risky choice and central-bank monetary policy, OptScientist discovers compact symbolic optimization laws that achieve held-out predictive performance competitive with leading baselines, while using few parameters and substantially fewer tokens than LLM baselines. Overall, OptScientist extends automated scientific discovery to uncovering optimization laws that generate observed phenomena, enabling automated theory building across the physical, biological, behavioral, and social sciences.

items.title_en: Convergence of stochastic gradient descent for learning linear neural networks
items.title_zh: 学习线性神经网络时随机梯度下降的收敛性
items.abstract_en: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is the cornerstone of modern deep learning, yet its theoretical convergence properties remain poorly understood in non-convex settings. To address this gap, we study SGD dynamics in deep linear neural networks - simplified models that retain key non-convex characteristics while remaining analytically tractable. Building on recent results for gradient descent, we extend convergence guarantees to SGD under regularized squared loss. We establish almost sure boundedness of SGD iterates. Using the framework of asymptotic pseudotrajectories from stochastic approximation theory, our analysis establishes then, for both deterministic and adaptive step-size choices, convergence of SGD to the set of critical points under mild conditions (without relying on Lipschitz properties or whitened data). To our knowledge, this is the first work providing almost sure convergence guarantees for SGD in deep linear networks, bridging the gap between theoretical optimization and practical stochastic training.

items.title_en: When Do LLMs Help with Feature Selection? A Systematic Empirical Study
items.title_zh: LLMs 何时有助于特征选择？一项系统性的实证研究
items.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) can leverage semantic feature names alongside summary statistics for tabular feature selection, yet it remains unclear when such information improves subset selection relative to established statistical methods. We investigate this question within an 18-dataset framework comprising 10 datasets for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training, 2 for checkpoint validation, and 6 held-out evaluation datasets. We compare five classical baselines, frozen Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.3-70B selectors, and two GRPO-adapted Qwen2.5-7B models, reporting classification ROC-AUC and regression R^2 separately and using dataset-wise ranks for cross-task comparison. Across five seeded evaluation partitions, classical selectors generally achieve higher predictive performance than the tested 7B LLM/RL selectors, including under a pre-specified ~33% feature budget with strict train-only classical fitting, while the 7B selectors retain compact subsets. A cardinality-matched semantic sensitivity experiment shows that, for Zero-shot Qwen-7B, informative feature names improve regression performance over anonymized and shuffled alternatives (+0.1964 and +0.1606 mean R^2), whereas aggregate classification differences are smaller (+0.0159 and +0.0084 ROC-AUC) and dataset-dependent. These results characterize when semantic information benefits LLM-based feature selection and show that classical selectors remain strong baselines for predictive tabular feature selection.

items.title_en: Learning Computational Structure for Sample-Efficient Prediction
items.title_zh: 面向样本高效预测的学习计算结构
items.abstract_en: Statistical learning in high dimensions suffers from the curse of dimensionality. Fortunately, many functions of practical interest are compositionally sparse, meaning they admit a composition of local functions, each depending on only a few variables, allowing sample complexity to depend on local arity rather than ambient dimension. Yet realizing this benefit requires exploiting hidden compositional structure, which theory does not establish for practical gradient-based training. We study this gap with CSFRBench, a controlled benchmark that hides the target's compositional computation during training but retains it for diagnosis, and find that dense networks and sparsity-based baselines leave much of that benefit unrealized. Inspired by the spatial organization of biological neural circuits, we introduce Learned Wiring (LeWi): each neuron has a learned low-dimensional embedding, only nearby neurons connect, and embeddings and weights are trained jointly. LeWi improves sample efficiency on targets with hierarchical structure, intermediate reuse, or independent modules. Across 32 additional targets generated by independently sampled computation graphs, LeWi is the most sample-efficient method not given the target graph, with 27% lower mean learning-curve area than dense networks. Dense networks perform better on targets with a single high-arity function. LeWi's representations and connectivity align with the target computation. On 17 world-model prediction tasks spanning control, navigation, and manipulation, LeWi beats the dense baseline on 16 and wins 99/119 baseline comparisons. These results show that jointly learning connectivity and weights can exploit computational structure to improve sample efficiency.

items.title_en: Discount Yourself: Self-inclusive Freshness-weighted Gossip for Decentralised Learning under Client Outages
items.title_zh: 自我折扣：客户端中断下去中心化学习的自包含新鲜度加权 Gossip
items.abstract_en: Decentralised federated learning (DFL) trains personalised models on devices that average with their neighbours rather than with a central server. Real devices, however, are often offline for hours or days, and a client returning from an outage can recover only by aggregating the models its neighbourhood holds. We observe that the stalest of these models is usually the client's own, a case that existing staleness-aware rules, which discount only the models a client receives, do not address. We formalise aggregation after an outage as estimating the state of a fully available network and derive three principles. First, the receiver must be discounted like any neighbour. Every rule that weights it at least as much as each neighbour has an error that grows without bound with the outage, whereas discounting all candidates by relative staleness keeps the error bounded. Second, staleness must be measured as inherited lag rather than age, since local training resets a model's age but not the lag it absorbed from stale neighbours. We introduce the effective lag, which tracks this quantity at the cost of one scalar per message. Third, the discount must be steep, because absorbed lag persists in every later round. These principles define Self-inclusive Freshness-weighted Gossip (SFG), a family of drop-in aggregation rules with the communication and computation of decentralised federated averaging, whose guarantees hold for the stale receiver itself. On three image benchmarks and eight outage processes, including real smartphone availability traces, the lag-based members SFG-L and SFG-Cut consistently outperform decentralised federated averaging and recent age-of-information rules, and ablations show that each principle is necessary. The analysis also explains why tuned limited merging from gossip learning is effective.

items.title_en: Binary Discrete Diffusion: Candidate-Set Diffusion for Logic and Planning Tasks
items.title_zh: 二元离散扩散：面向逻辑与规划任务的候选集扩散
items.abstract_en: Discrete diffusion models iteratively denoise a noisy sequence of categorical data such as text, enabling any-order generation with self-correction and in-filling capabilities. This makes them promising candidates for reasoning, planning, and constrained-generation tasks like coding and math. Yet masked and uniform diffusion erase a token's identity in a single corruption event, so their noisy states cannot explicitly represent partially resolved uncertainty in which several alternatives remain plausible. We close this gap with Binary Discrete Diffusion, a family of continuous-time discrete-diffusion processes whose noisy state is a set of candidate tokens per position, represented as a binary membership vector. Binary diffusion changes candidate sets through additions and removals, allowing information to be lost and recovered gradually while the diffusion state itself represents partial uncertainty. On Sudoku-Extreme, Boxoban, and graph coloring, the symmetric formulation of binary diffusion consistently outperforms strong, well-tuned masked and uniform baselines under matched architectures and controlled training, sampling, and tuning budgets, with its largest gains on the hardest instances, while remaining competitive on language modeling (Text8, TinyStories, OpenWebText). These results support candidate sets as an effective intermediate representation for iterative reasoning and show that the corruption kernel can materially change the computation learned by the reverse model.

items.title_en: GraphCast-Mamba: Learning Non-Markovian Corrections for Weather Forecasting
items.title_zh: GraphCast-Mamba：为天气预报学习非马尔可夫修正
items.abstract_en: Unresolved atmospheric processes can introduce history dependence beyond the short input windows used by many weather forecasting models. We introduce GraphCast--Mamba, which augments a frozen, pretrained $1^\circ$ GraphCast backbone with a trainable Mamba correction branch combining graph message passing and Mamba layers. The branch retains a temporal memory state across successive six-hour forecast steps, learning corrections informed by temporal context beyond GraphCast's two-frame input. Training is confined to the correction branch, using ERA5 data from 2015--2021. After 2,500 optimizer updates, including warm-up, the selected model achieves substantial improvements relative to the uncorrected GraphCast backbone. It reduces the GraphCast loss (normalized weighted mean-squared error; MSE) by 14.42% when aggregated over the full ten-day forecast and by 21.66% at day 10 (240 h after forecast initialization). At this final forecast lead time, root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreases by 7.09--14.60% across all 11 evaluated variable groups, spanning temperature, wind, pressure, geopotential, specific humidity, and precipitation. These results demonstrate broad improvements in ten-day weather forecasts through a short correction-training schedule while retaining the pretrained backbone.

items.title_en: Variance Reduction with Delayed Feedback for Non-Convex Optimization
items.abstract_en: We study variance reduction for non-convex optimization when gradient evaluations return with a delay. The server can update the parameter while earlier evaluations remain unfinished. We first analyze an ordered recursive momentum estimator for stochastic optimization. Under average smoothness and bounded variance, its oracle complexity is $O(1+σ^2ε^{-2}+LΔ_f(1+σ/ε+τ)ε^{-2})$, where the target is an expected squared gradient norm of at most $ε^2$ and $τ$ bounds the feedback delay. We next study finite sums with $n$ components and obtain $O(n+LΔ_f(\sqrt n+\min\{τ,n-1\})ε^{-2})$ evaluations. An asynchronous snapshot variant continues updating during full-gradient computations under an explicit bound on their completion time. For the stochastic method, we further replace a maximum-delay bound by a bound on the weighted amount of missing feedback.

items.title_en: ECG for laboratory values:A comprehensive physiological and technical analysis
items.title_zh: 用心电图预测化验指标：生理与技术的综合分析
items.abstract_en: Laboratory measurements are essential for clinical decision making but typically require invasive blood sampling. Recent research suggests that ECG recordings may contain information beyond cardiac rhythm and provide information related to laboratory values. This thesis investigates NT-proBNP prediction from ECG recordings and patient metadata using a multimodal deep learning framework, while considering the physiological plausibility of ECG-based prediction. It also compares a 1-lead configuration using lead II with the corresponding 12-lead configuration. Additional experiments on glucose, hemoglobin, and potassium are presented in the appendix. Regression, binary classification, and three-class classification experiments were conducted using MIMIC-IV, with the three-class task based on clinically established thresholds. The 12-lead configuration consistently achieved better performance. Regression reached a mean absolute error of 534.98 pg/mL for 1-lead and 514.27 pg/mL for 12-lead. Binary classification achieved AUROCs of 0.849 and 0.876, respectively, while three-class classification achieved macro-averaged AUROCs of 0.738 and 0.752. The results indicate that precise NT-proBNP regression remains challenging, whereas broader concentration ranges can be classified more effectively. The findings are consistent with the physiological hypothesis that ECG characteristics and NT-proBNP concentrations reflect shared cardiovascular processes. ECG-based NT-proBNP prediction may therefore provide complementary information, particularly for classifying broader concentration ranges. However, laboratory measurements remain necessary, and validation on independent datasets is required.
items.abstract_zh: 实验室检测对临床决策至关重要，但通常需要采血。近期研究表明，心电图（ECG）可能携带心律之外的信息，与部分化验值相关。本论文用多模态深度学习框架，结合ECG记录与患者元数据预测NT-proBNP，并考察ECG预测的生理合理性；同时比较仅用II导联的单导联配置与对应12导联配置，附录还给出葡萄糖、血红蛋白与钾的实验。基于MIMIC-IV开展回归、二分类与三类分类（阈值取临床常用切点）实验。12导联一致更优：回归平均绝对误差单导联534.98 pg/mL、12导联514.27 pg/mL；二分类AUROC分别为0.849与0.876；三类分类宏平均AUROC为0.738与0.752。结果表明精确回归仍困难，但较宽的浓度区间可较好区分，与ECG特征和NT-proBNP反映共同心血管过程的生理假设一致。该方法或可提供互补信息，但化验检测仍不可替代，且需独立数据验证。
items.highlight_zh: ECG可较准判断NT-proBNP浓度区间，精确回归仍难
items.digest_zh:
① 研究问题：抽血化验有创、费时、需要设备和人力。心电图便宜、易得、无创，能否“顺手”从心电波形里推断出一些常见化验指标？
② 方法：使用公开重症数据集MIMIC-IV，把ECG波形与患者元数据一起输入多模态深度学习模型，预测心衰标志物NT-proBNP；任务包括回归（预测具体数值）、二分类和三分类（按临床常用阈值划分浓度区间）。同时比较只用II导联的单导联配置与完整12导联配置。附录还把同样的思路用到血糖、血红蛋白和血钾上。
③ 结果：12导联始终优于单导联。回归的平均绝对误差约515 pg/mL，说明精确数值很难估准；但二分类AUROC约0.88、三分类宏平均AUROC约0.75，说明判断“大致落在哪个浓度区间”是可行的。
④ 生理层面的解释：作者强调这不只是数据巧合——ECG的形态学改变与NT-proBNP升高都反映同一套心血管病理过程（如心室负荷增加、心肌肥厚），所以二者存在共享信息是合理的。
⑤ 意义与局限：ECG预测可作为补充信息，帮助筛查或辅助判断；但实验室检测仍然必需，替代不了抽血，而且结论还需在独立数据集上验证才能推广。

items.title_en: BitMTP: When Multi-Token Prediction Meets Low-Bit Large Language Models
items.abstract_en: For efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs), methods of ultra-low-bit backbones reduce weight storage, memory traffic, and linear-layer execution cost, while multi-token prediction (MTP) methods reduce sequential decoding steps by predicting multiple future tokens in parallel. Although complementary, the direct combination of these methods cannot accelerate decoding at comparable quality: masked drafting lacks intermediate token input supplied in next-token training, while wider computation and causal key-value (KV) updates can offset the savings from fewer steps. To address these challenges, we propose BitMTP, an algorithm-system co-design framework for efficient MTP on ultra-low-bit LLM backbones. A joint next-token prediction and MTP objective equips a single model with both autoregressive (AR) generation and block-causal drafting. Confidence-only decoding, speculative-only decoding, and hybrid decoding provide different quality-throughput operating points without using separate draft and verifier models. Accepted-prefix alignment keeps the committed prefix, materialized causal KV boundary, and CUDA Graph replay state consistent for continued generation. BitMTP uses this contract to select width-specialized low-bit execution and reuse captured graphs over shared KV storage. On NVIDIA H20, BitMTP with hybrid decoding achieves five-task mean speedups of 2.2x on BitNet b1.58-2B and 2.1-2.4x on 1.7B-4B Bonsai models at comparable task quality. On RTX 3090 and Jetson Orin, it further achieves up to 2.0x in five-task mean throughput and 3.3x on MBPP+, respectively. These results demonstrate that BitMTP accelerates ultra-low-bit LLM generation across backbones, model sizes, and GPU types. The source code is released at https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/BitMTP

items.title_en: Present but Hard to Read: Probing Latent Reasoning with Minimal Pairs
items.abstract_en: Probing studies of latent reasoning often read a model's state where the answer begins and take a failed probe as evidence that a value is absent. We test this with a digit copied from the question, in the looped model Ouro-1.4B and the standard transformer Qwen2.5-1.5B. Comparing prompts that differ only in that digit shows it is present at the last prompt token, in a code shared across questions (readout about 0.9). A probe that sees one prompt at a time, the usual setting, barely reads it: 0.36 in Ouro and 0.19 in Qwen even after 5,249 training questions. The digit's change is small rather than crowded: random noise lands on equally busy directions, while a random word in its place moves the state far more and is readable. Since every varied token leaves a trace, a successful probe is ambiguous too. We give a protocol, including a synthetic null for generic mixing, for testing computed values against copies and mixtures of the inputs. In pre-registered studies of two-step problems it finds a small signal for the unwritten intermediate a+b just before Ouro writes the answer's last digit, and its sign follows the operation, though mixing alone produces much of that sign-following part. Holding that value at another problem's from the first loop on does not move the written digit toward the other problem's, while the same patch of the answer does: the value is readable but not used.

items.title_en: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
items.title_zh: 基于SSM的脉冲神经网络的模型级与层级闭环预测
items.abstract_en: Deep State-Space Models (Deep SSMs) have shown promising performance and computational benefits in processing of time-series data with complex temporal dependencies. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) constitute a biologically inspired class of deep SSMs, where computing blocks communicate through spikes, discrete single-bit events rather than continuous activation functions. A particularly important task in time-series processing is forecasting, i.e. predicting future values of a sequence from past observations alone. However, how to best perform forecasting with SNNs is an open question, where the standard autoregressive nature of the data processing with SNNs requires values that are not available during the forecasting phase. In this article, we address this challenge. We explore two closed-loop forecasting strategies, in which the network's own generated values are fed back into the network as if they were observed past values: (i) model-level and (ii) layer-level closed-loop forecasting. We evaluate these approaches on the ETT-small datasets, a standard benchmark for time-series forecasting, under both spike-based and continuous activation functions. We compare the proposed closed-loop approaches against state-of-the-art methods such as SpaceTime, as well as the zero-masking baseline in S4. Both of the proposed approaches perform comparably to or better than zero-masking with S4, and in most cases match SpaceTime. These findings highlight the trade-off between continuous and low-bit quantized activations, and demonstrate that the proposed Deep SSM architectures provide a competitive framework for forecasting.

items.title_en: Geometry-Agnostic Data-Driven Discovery of Extreme Scenarios
items.abstract_en: We introduce a two-stage data-driven neural framework for discovering dynamically admissible extreme scenarios. Rather than assuming prior knowledge of the governing equations, the first stage infers the effective dynamical constraints directly from observational data. When the underlying physical system possesses suitable symmetries, the learned dynamics can be represented in a geometry-agnostic form, independent of any fixed grid, coordinate system, dimensionality, and intrinsic curvature. In the second stage, a physics-informed neural-search uses this learned dynamics to uncover rare, high-impact coherent structures that may not have appeared in the original observations. We demonstrate this framework through representative examples of increasing dimensionality and geometric complexity. Starting from a traditionally learned Duffing dynamics, we find a homoclinic pulse as a plausible localized extreme scenario. Next, since the same equation also appears in the stationary nonlinear Schrodinger system, with the coordinate interpreted as space instead of time, this pulse becomes a standing soliton. We then retrain the first stage using a geometry-agnostic neural representation, enabling the learned dynamics to be lifted to higher-dimensional space to obtain higher-dimensional solitary profile, known as Townes soliton. Finally, with a Liouville system, we demonstrate that dynamics learned from data on a (1+1)-dimensional Lorentzian quasi-manifold can be transferred to a (2+0)-dimensional Euclidean manifold to identify an instanton. Our approach can be applied to other coherent spatiotemporal structures, including kinks, rogue waves, compactons, peakons, and potentially even singularities, with applications in risk analysis, nonlinear forecasting, and anomaly detection.

items.title_en: Claims of emergence in AI should be grounded in information decomposition
items.abstract_en: When a language model develops capabilities not traceable to its individual components, when a multi-agent AI system outperforms each agent on its own, or when a human-AI pair succeeds where either fails in isolation, AI researchers describe it as a case of ``synergy'' or ``emergence''. However, these are usually informal assessments not supported by a theoretical framework, making these claims impossible to compare or even meaningfully dispute.
